## Question 1: Automatic Model Discovery for Custom Providers

**Yes, 9router has extensive automatic model discovery**, but it works differently for built-in providers vs. custom provider nodes.

### Built-in Providers: Live `/models` Fetching

The file `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/app/api/providers/[id]/models/route.js` contains a comprehensive `PROVIDER_MODELS_CONFIG` map (lines ~120-450) with live model-fetching configurations for **40+ providers**. Each entry specifies:
- The upstream `/models` endpoint URL
- Auth headers/query params
- Response parsers (`parseOpenAIStyleModels`, `parseCodexModels`, etc.)
- OAuth token refresh-on-401 via `buildOAuthResolver()`

Examples from the config:
```js
openai: createOpenAIModelsConfig("https://api.openai.com/v1/models"),
deepseek: createOpenAIModelsConfig("https://api.deepseek.com/models"),
groq: createOpenAIModelsConfig("https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models"),
ollama: createOpenAIModelsConfig("https://ollama.com/api/tags"),
```

Providers with non-standard APIs get `customResolver` functions (kiro, qoder, cursor, kimchi, grok-cli, gemini-cli, codex, ollama-local). These handle OAuth refresh, proprietary endpoints, and fallback to static catalogs.

### Custom Provider Nodes: Two Discovery Mechanisms

**Mechanism A — Validation-time discovery** (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/app/api/provider-nodes/validate/route.js`):
When a user adds a custom OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible provider node, the validation endpoint hits `{baseUrl}/models` to verify connectivity. If that fails, it falls back to testing `{baseUrl}/chat/completions` with a ping message. This validates the provider but doesn't persist the model list.

**Mechanism B — Dashboard live fetch** (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/app/api/providers/[id]/models/route.js`, lines ~460-530):
For custom provider connections (OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible), the GET handler fetches `{baseUrl}/models` using the stored API key:
```js
if (isOpenAICompatibleProvider(connection.provider)) {
  const url = `${baseUrl.replace(/\/$/, "")}/models`;
  const response = await fetch(url, {
    headers: { "Authorization": `Bearer ${connection.apiKey}` },
  });
  // ... returns parsed models
}
```

**Mechanism C — Suggested models** (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/shared/utils/providerModelsFetcher.js` + `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/app/api/providers/suggested-models/route.js`):
A client-side fetcher with 10-minute in-memory cache that proxies through `/api/providers/suggested-models?url=...&type=...`. The backend fetches the URL, parses with type-specific filters from `filters.js`, and returns filtered model lists. Used in the dashboard UI to populate model dropdowns.

### Static Config: `providerModels.js`

`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/open-sse/config/providerModels.js` is **not** a hardcoded model list. It re-exports `PROVIDER_MODELS` from `open-sse/providers/index.js`, which is built from the provider registry (`open-sse/providers/registry/`). This serves as the **fallback catalog** when live fetching fails. Functions like `isValidModel()`, `getModelTargetFormat()`, and `findModelName()` use this static registry for routing decisions.

### Custom Models Storage

Custom models added by users are stored in the DB via `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/lib/db/repos/aliasRepo.js` (line 22: `customModels: key=${providerAlias}|${id}|${type}`). The API at `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/app/api/models/custom/route.js` handles add/delete.

## Question 2: Automatic Fallback Chains

**Yes, 9router has a sophisticated multi-layer fallback system** with three distinct mechanisms:

### Layer 1: Combo Model Fallback (Multi-Model)

**Entry point:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/sse/handlers/chat.js` (lines 89-131)

When a request uses a combo name (e.g., `"my-combo"` instead of `"openai/gpt-4"`), the system:
1. Calls `getComboModels(modelStr)` to resolve the combo into an array of models
2. Detects required capabilities (vision, pdf, audio) via `detectRequiredCapabilities(body)`
3. Reorders models by capability fit via `reorderByCapabilities()`
4. Selects strategy: `"fallback"`, `"round-robin"`, or `"fusion"`

**Core engine:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/open-sse/services/combo.js` (lines 260-370)

`handleComboChat()` iterates through models sequentially:
```js
for (let i = 0; i < rotatedModels.length; i++) {
  const result = await handleSingleModel(body, modelStr);
  if (result.ok) return result;  // Success → done

  const { shouldFallback, cooldownMs } = checkFallbackError(result.status, errorText);
  if (!shouldFallback) return result;  // Non-retryable error → stop

  // For transient 503/502/504, wait before falling through
  if (cooldownMs > 0 && cooldownMs <= 5000) {
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, cooldownMs));
  }
  // Continue to next model
}
```

**Round-robin rotation** with sticky limits: `getRotatedModels()` tracks per-combo rotation state in memory (`comboRotationState` Map), advancing the index after N consecutive requests (configurable via `comboStickyRoundRobinLimit`).

**Fusion strategy**: Sends the same request to multiple models simultaneously and uses a judge model to pick the best response.

### Layer 2: Multi-Account Fallback (Same Provider, Different Credentials)

**Entry point:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/sse/handlers/chat.js` (lines 222-260)

Even for single-model requests, there's an account-selection loop:
```js
const excludeConnectionIds = new Set();
while (true) {
  const credentials = await getProviderCredentials(provider, excludeConnectionIds, model);
  if (!credentials || credentials.allRateLimited) { /* return error */ }

  const result = await chatCore(...);
  if (success) return result;

  excludeConnectionIds.add(credentials.connectionId);  // Exclude failed account
  // Loop continues with next account
}
```

**Account selection logic:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/sse/services/auth.js` (lines 27-120)

`getProviderCredentials()` implements:
- **Mutex-protected** selection to prevent race conditions
- **Model-level locking**: Per-model rate limit locks via `isModelLockActive(c, model)` using flat fields `modelLock_${model}` on connection records
- **Strategy-based selection**: `"fill-first"` (use one account until exhausted) vs. other strategies, configurable per-provider via `settings.providerStrategies`
- **Exponential backoff tracking**: Tracks `rateLimitedUntil` timestamps per account
- **Free provider injection**: Virtual no-auth connections for free-tier providers

### Layer 3: Token Refresh Retry

**In:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js` (lines 370-393)

When a request gets a 401/token error:
```js
const newCredentials = await refreshWithRetry(async () => {
  // Attempt token refresh
});
if (newCredentials) {
  const retryResult = await executor.execute({ ...credentials: newCredentials });
  if (retryResult.response.ok) { /* use refreshed response */ }
}
```

### Error Classification for Fallback Decisions

`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/open-sse/config/errorConfig.js` defines `ERROR_RULES` checked top-to-bottom:
- **Text-based**: "rate limit", "too many requests", "quota exceeded", "overloaded" → exponential backoff
- **Status-based**: 429 → backoff; 401/402/403/404 → long cooldown (2 min)
- **Default**: 30s transient cooldown for unmatched errors

Backoff formula: `base(2s) × 2^level`, max 5 minutes, max 15 levels.

### Capacity Adapter Auto-Switch

Even single-model requests get auto-augmented: if a request needs vision but the target model lacks it, `augmentModelsWithCapacityAdapter()` inserts a capable model as a fallback (lines 135-155 in `chat.js`).

---

**Summary:**
- **Model Discovery**: ✅ Automatic for both built-in (live API fetch + static fallback) and custom providers (validation-time + dashboard fetch + suggested models cache)
- **Fallback Chains**: ✅ Three layers — combo model fallback, multi-account rotation, and token refresh retry — all driven by config-driven error classification

Great news — 9router already has both capabilities you're asking about, and they're quite sophisticated. Here's the breakdown:

---

## 1. Automatic Model Discovery for Custom Providers ✅

When you add a custom provider, 9router **does** automatically fetch available models. There are three mechanisms:

- **At validation time** (`src/app/api/provider-nodes/validate/route.js`): When you first add a custom OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible provider, it hits `{baseUrl}/models` to verify connectivity and discover models.
- **Dashboard live fetch** (`src/app/api/providers/[id]/models/route.js`): The dashboard calls `{baseUrl}/models` using your stored API key whenever you view or select models for a custom provider. This works for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- **Suggested models with caching** (`src/shared/utils/providerModelsFetcher.js`): A client-side fetcher with a 10-minute in-memory cache that populates model dropdowns in the UI.

For the **40+ built-in providers**, there's an even richer system with per-provider parsers, OAuth token refresh on 401, and fallback to static catalogs when live fetching fails.

**Bottom line:** If your custom provider exposes an OpenAI-compatible `/models` endpoint, 9router will auto-discover models from it. No manual model entry needed.

---

## 2. Automatic Fallback Chains ✅ (Three Layers Deep)

This is exactly what you want — your client app never needs to worry about picking a backup model. 9router handles it transparently:

### Layer 1: Combo Model Fallback
You define a **combo** (a named list of models like `"my-combo" → [openai/gpt-4o, anthropic/claude-sonnet, deepseek/chat]`). When a request uses that combo name:
- Models are tried **sequentially** — if one fails with a retryable error (429, 503, 502, 504, overloaded), it falls through to the next
- Supports **round-robin** rotation across requests (with sticky limits)
- Even supports **fusion** mode (send to multiple models simultaneously, judge picks the best)
- Capability-aware reordering: if the request needs vision/PDF/audio, capable models are prioritized

### Layer 2: Multi-Account Fallback
Even for a **single model** request, if you have multiple API keys/accounts for the same provider:
- Failed accounts are excluded and the next account is tried automatically
- Rate-limit tracking with exponential backoff per account
- Model-level locking so a rate-limited model doesn't burn all accounts
- Mutex-protected to prevent race conditions

### Layer 3: Token Refresh Retry
On 401/token errors, 9router automatically refreshes OAuth tokens and retries before falling back.

### Error Classification
The system in `open-sse/config/errorConfig.js` classifies errors intelligently:
- **"rate limit", "too many requests", "quota exceeded"** → exponential backoff (2s × 2^level, max 5 min)
- **429** → backoff; **401/403** → longer cooldown
- **Transient server errors** → short cooldown then retry

---

## What This Means For You

Your client application can simply send requests to 9router's `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint using a **combo name** as the model string, and 9router will:

1. Try each model in the combo until one succeeds
2. Rotate across multiple API keys per provider
3. Refresh expired tokens automatically
4. Never return a failure unless *every* option is exhausted

**No client-side retry logic needed.** Just configure your combos in the dashboard and point your app at 9router.

Here is the complete architectural analysis of the 9router combo/virtual model infrastructure and how a smart router could be built on top of it.

## 1. Combo System Architecture

### Data Model
**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/lib/db/schema.js` (lines 89-98)
```js
combos: {
  columns: {
    id: "TEXT PRIMARY KEY",
    name: "TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL",   // ← this is what users put in body.model
    kind: "TEXT",                    // optional discriminator
    models: "TEXT NOT NULL",         // JSON array of "provider/model" strings
    createdAt: "TEXT NOT NULL",
    updatedAt: "TEXT NOT NULL",
  },
}
```

**Repo:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/lib/db/repos/combosRepo.js`
- `getComboByName(name)` — lookup by exact name match
- `createCombo({ name, kind, models })` — models stored as JSON string
- Combos are **user-defined at runtime** via the dashboard, not hardcoded

### Model Resolution Flow
**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/sse/services/model.js`

The resolution order in `getModelInfo(modelStr)`:
1. **Parse** `modelStr` → if it contains `/`, split into `provider/model`
2. **If no `/`** → treat as alias or combo name
3. **Check combos first** (`getComboByName`) → if found, return `{ provider: null, model: name }` (null provider signals combo handling)
4. **Check model aliases** from DB
5. **Check provider nodes** (user-defined OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoints)
6. **Fallback:** infer provider from model name prefix (`claude-` → anthropic, `gpt-` → openai, etc.)

**Critical insight:** A model string WITHOUT a `/` is checked against combos BEFORE aliases. This means combo names take priority.

---

## 2. Combo Strategies (3 modes)

**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/open-sse/services/combo.js`

### Strategy Selection
**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/sse/handlers/chat.js` (lines 90-130)
```js
const comboStrategies = settings.comboStrategies || {};
const comboSpecificStrategy = comboStrategies[modelStr]?.fallbackStrategy;
const comboStrategy = comboSpecificStrategy || settings.comboStrategy || "fallback";
```
Per-combo overrides live in `settings.comboStrategies[name].fallbackStrategy`. Global default in `settings.comboStrategy`.

### Fallback (default)
Tries models in order. On retryable error (429, 503, 502, 504), waits optional cooldown then falls through. Returns first 2xx response. Non-retryable errors (400, 401, 403) stop immediately.

### Round-Robin
`getRotatedModels()` maintains per-combo rotation state in an in-memory `Map<string, {index, consecutiveUseCount}>`. Respects `comboStickyRoundRobinLimit` (N requests per model before rotating). State resets on combo/settings change via `resetComboRotation()`.

### Fusion
`handleFusionChat()` — the most sophisticated strategy:
1. **Fan-out:** Sends request to ALL panel models in parallel (non-streaming, tools stripped, tool history flattened to prose)
2. **Quorum-grace collection:** Waits for `minPanel` successes, then gives stragglers `stragglerGraceMs` (default 8s), hard-capped at `panelHardTimeoutMs` (90s)
3. **Judge synthesis:** Appends anonymized panel responses as a new user turn with a detailed judge prompt analyzing consensus/contradictions/blind spots, then calls the judge model (defaults to panel[0], overridable via `comboStrategies[name].judgeModel`)
4. **Graceful degradation:** 0 answers → 503; 1 answer → return directly without fusion

---

## 3. Capability Detection & Auto-Switch

**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/open-sse/services/combo.js`

### `detectRequiredCapabilities(body)`
Scans ONLY the **trailing user turn** (messages after last assistant turn) for:
- `vision` — image_url, image, input_image blocks, image/* mime
- `pdf` — file/document blocks without specific mime
- `audioInput` — input_audio, audio/* mime
- `videoInput` — input_video, video/* mime

Supports OpenAI messages, Claude messages, Gemini contents, and OpenAI Responses API input formats.

### `reorderByCapabilities(models, required)`
Stable 3-tier sort:
- **Tier 0:** Satisfies ALL hard + soft caps
- **Tier 1:** Satisfies all hard caps only
- **Tier 2:** Missing at least one hard cap

Hard caps: `vision`, `pdf`, `audioInput`, `videoInput` (missing = data loss). Never drops models, just reorders.

### Integration Point
In `handleComboChat()`, auto-switch runs AFTER rotation but BEFORE the fallback loop:
```js
if (autoSwitch) {
  const required = detectRequiredCapabilities(body);
  if (required.size > 0) {
    rotatedModels = reorderByCapabilities(rotatedModels, required);
  }
}
```

---

## 4. Capacity Adapter System

**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/open-sse/services/capacityAdapter.js`

This is essentially a **global capability-based fallback pool** that works even for single-model requests:

### How It Works
1. Settings define per-capability model pools: `settings.capacityAdapter.vision.models`, `.pdf.models`, etc.
2. `augmentModelsWithCapacityAdapter(models, requiredCaps, settings)`:
   - If ANY original model satisfies all hard caps → returns original list unchanged
   - If NONE satisfy → **prepends** capable pool models as priority candidates
3. `withCapacityAdapterStripping(handleSingleModel, adapterModels)` wraps the callback to strip conversation history for adapter models with smaller context windows (`stripHistoryForContext`)

### Key Detail
The capacity adapter also applies to **single model requests** (not just combos):
```js
// src/sse/handlers/chat.js lines 135-147
const soloAugmented = augmentModelsWithCapacityAdapter([modelStr], requiredCapabilities, settings);
if (soloAugmented.length > 1) {
  // Promotes to combo-style fallback automatically
  return handleComboChat({ body, models: soloAugmented, ... });
}
```

---

## 5. Provider Registry System

**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/open-sse/providers/index.js`

Providers register via static imports in `open-sse/providers/registry/index.js` (auto-generated, 100 providers). Each registry entry provides:
- `id` / `alias` / `aliases[]`
- `transport` (format, baseUrl, auth type)
- `models[]` (normalized via `normalizeModel`)
- Optional: `oauth`, media configs

`PROVIDER_MODELS` is keyed by alias (or id if no alias). Model validation uses `isValidModel(aliasOrId, modelId)`.

### Capabilities System
**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/open-sse/providers/capabilities.js`

4-layer fallback:
1. `PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES[provider][model]` — provider-specific override
2. `MODEL_CAPABILITIES[model]` — exact id exceptions
3. `PATTERN_CAPABILITIES` — glob patterns, ordered specific→generic
4. `DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES` — safe floor (200K context, 64K output, tools:true)

---

## 6. Request Body Flow Through Combo Resolution

```
Client POST /v1/chat/completions { model: "my-combo", messages: [...] }

src/sse/handlers/chat.js :: handleChat()
  ├─ Parse body, extract modelStr
  ├─ detectRequiredCapabilities(body)     ← scans trailing user turn
  ├─ getComboModels(modelStr)             ← DB lookup by name
  │   └─ Found? → combo path
  │       ├─ Read strategy from settings.comboStrategies[name]
  │       ├─ augmentModelsWithCapacityAdapter(comboModels, caps, settings)
  │       ├─ If fusion → handleFusionChat(...)
  │       └─ Else → handleComboChat(...)
  │           ├─ getRotatedModels()       ← round-robin state
  │           ├─ reorderByCapabilities()  ← auto-switch
  │           └─ Fallback loop → handleSingleModelChat() for each
  │               ├─ getModelInfo(modelStr) → {provider, model}
  │               ├─ getProviderCredentials(provider)
  │               ├─ checkAndRefreshToken()
  │               └─ handleChatCore() → translator → executor → upstream
  └─ Not a combo? → single model path
      ├─ augmentModelsWithCapacityAdapter([modelStr], ...)
      └─ handleSingleModelChat() directly
```

## 7. Smart Router Design: Feasibility Analysis

### Option A: Register `9router` as a Virtual Provider ✅ RECOMMENDED

Create `open-sse/providers/registry/9router.js`:
```js
export default {
  id: "9router",
  alias: "9r",
  transport: { format: "openai", baseUrl: "http://localhost:20128/v1" },
  models: [
    { id: "auto", name: "Auto (Smart Router)" },
    { id: "best-code", name: "Best Code Model" },
    { id: "best-chat", name: "Best Chat Model" },
    { id: "best-reasoning", name: "Best Reasoning" },
  ],
};
```

**Why this works cleanly:**
- `parseModel("9router/auto")` → `{ provider: "9router", model: "auto" }` — standard parsing, no special cases
- The executor (`open-sse/executors/9router.js`) would contain the smart routing logic
- It can call back into `handleComboChat` or `handleSingleModelChat` internally with the selected real model
- Capabilities system can declare what each virtual model supports
- No changes needed to combo resolution, model parsing, or the chat handler

**The executor pattern:** Look at how `open-sse/executors/perplexity-web.js` maps `"pplx-auto"` to specific models, or how `open-sse/executors/qoder.js` maps canonical keys (`auto`, `ultimate`) to real upstream models. Your `9router` executor would do the same but with task-analysis-driven selection.

### Option B: Special Prefix Without Provider Registration
Use bare names like `auto` or `smart/gpt-4-class`. **Problems:**
- `auto` without `/` gets treated as a combo name first → conflicts with user combos
- `smart/gpt-4-class` would need `smart` registered as a provider anyway
- Less clean than Option A

### Option C: Extend Combo System with Dynamic Combos
Add a `kind: "smart"` to combos and intercept in `handleChat`. **Problems:**
- Combos have a fixed model list; smart routing needs dynamic selection
- Would require modifying `getComboModels` to return dynamic results
- Mixes two concerns (static fallback groups vs intelligent routing)

### Hooks Available for Custom Routing Logic

1. **Pre-combo hook point** in `handleChat()` (line ~88): Before `getComboModels()`, you could intercept specific model strings
2. **Inside the executor**: A `9router` executor has full access to the request body, can analyze messages, and dispatch to any real provider
3. **Capacity adapter pattern**: `augmentModelsWithCapacityAdapter()` shows how to dynamically inject models based on request analysis — your smart router could use a similar augmentation step
4. **Settings integration**: `settings.comboStrategies[name]` already supports per-combo config objects — a smart router config could specify weights, preferences, analysis depth

### Recommended Architecture

```
Client sends: { model: "9router/auto", messages: [...] }

handleChat() → parseModel → provider:"9router", model:"auto"

handleSingleModelChat() → getProviderCredentials("9router") → no real credentials needed

handleChatCore() → executor: open-sse/executors/9router.js

9router executor:
  1. Analyze messages (task type, complexity, modalities, code vs prose)
  2. Score available models using capabilities + pricing + latency data
  3. Select best model (or build a mini-combo for fallback)
  4. Call handleSingleModelChat(selectedRealModel) internally
  5. Return response (optionally adding X-9Router-Selected-rnally
  5. Return response  
```

The key files to modify/create:
- **Create:** `open-sse/providers/registry/9router.js` — virtual provider registration
- **Create:** `open-sse/executors/9router.js` — smart routing logic
- **Modify:** `open-sse/providers/registry/index.js` — add import (or run `scripts/migrate-registry.mjs`)
- **Optionally modify:** `open-sse/providers/capabilities.js` — add entries for `9router/auto` etc.
- **Optionally create:** `open-sse/services/smartRouter.js` — reusable task analysis + model scoring logic

**Fallback UI** — already functional at `/dashboard/combos`:

- Global round-robin settings on `/dashboard/profile`
- **Missing:** No LLM combo detail page (media combos have one), no test/playground for LLM combos, no smart router UI

**Combo Engine** — fully built in `open-sse/services/combo.js`:
- Sequential fallback, round-robin rotation, fusion (parallel + judge)
- Capability-aware reordering (`detectRequiredCapabilities` → `reorderByCapabilities`)

**Smart Router** — does NOT exist yet. OpenRouter's Auto Beta is the gold standard reference: lightweight task classifier → community spend-share ranking → cost/quality dial → session stickiness.

## 6. Runtime Error/Fallback Handling

**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/open-sse/services/combo.js`

### `handleComboChat()` (lines 261–340):
1. **Rotation**: Applies round-robin rotation via `getRotatedModels()` if strategy is `"round-robin"`
2. **Auto-switch by capability**: Calls `detectRequiredCapabilities(body)` → `reorderByCapabilities()` to float capable models to front (lines 270–279). This is the closest thing to "smart routing" — but it only considers **input modality** (vision, audio, pdf), NOT prompt content, cost, latency, or quality
3. **Sequential fallback loop**: Tries each model in order (lines 283–325)
   - On success (2xx): returns immediately
   - On error: calls `checkFallbackError(status, errorText)` to decide if fallback should continue
   - Transient errors (502/503/504): waits `cooldownMs` (up to 5s) before trying next
   - Non-fallback errors (e.g., 400 bad request): returns error immediately without trying next model
4. **All failed**: Returns 503 with last error message and earliest `retryAfter` header

### `handleFusionChat()` (lines 520–600):
- Fans out to all panel models in parallel (non-streaming, tools stripped)
- Uses quorum-grace collection: proceeds after `minPanel` successes + grace window
- Judge synthesizes one answer from anonymized panel responses
- Graceful degradation: 0 answers → 503, 1 answer → return directly without judging

### `reorderByCapabilities()` (lines 68–88):
- Tier 0: satisfies all hard + soft capabilities
- Tier 1: satisfies hard caps only
- Tier 2: missing hard caps
- Stable sort preserving original order within tiers

---

## 7. Gap Analysis: Existing vs. "modelRouter" Virtual Auto-Selecting Model

### What EXISTS:
| Feature | Status |
|---------|--------|
| Ordered model lists with fallback | ✅ Full CRUD + UI |
| Round-robin rotation | ✅ Per-combo configurable |
| Fusion (parallel panel + judge) | ✅ With judge selection + tuning |
| Capability-based auto-reorder | ✅ Vision/audio/pdf detection only |
| Capacity adapter (global fallback pools) | ✅ Per-modality model pools |
| Per-combo strategy override | ✅ Stored in settings |
| Error-aware fallback (transient wait) | ✅ 502/503/504 cooldown |

### What's MISSING for a true "modelRouter":
| Gap | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| **Content-aware routing** | No analysis of prompt content (coding, creative, reasoning, translation) to select optimal model |
| **Cost optimization** | No cost-per-token awareness; can't prefer cheaper models for simple queries |
| **Latency optimization** | No latency tracking or preference for faster models |
| **Quality scoring** | No historical success/quality metrics per model per task type |
| **Conditional rules engine** | No user-configurable "if X then use Y" routing rules |
| **Virtual model endpoint** | No `modelRouter` pseudo-model that acts as an auto-selecting proxy |
| **Token budget awareness** | Can't route based on remaining quota or spend limits |
| **A/B testing / experimentation** | No way to compare model performance on same prompts |
| **Drag-and-drop reordering** | ComboFormModal uses arrow buttons, not DnD (despite library being available) |
| **Test/playground** | No way to test a combo configuration before deploying |
| **Routing analytics** | No dashboard showing which models were selected, why, success rates |

### The closest existing primitive:
The **Capacity Adapter** + `reorderByCapabilities()` is the seed of smart routing — it already inspects request content and reorders models. But it only handles **input modality** (does the request contain images/audio?), not **task semantics** (is this a coding question?). A "modelRouter" would extend this pattern to analyze prompt intent and match against model strengths.

## 1. Request Flow: `handleChat()` → Model Resolution

**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/sse/handlers/chat.js`

### Resolution Order (lines 56–145)
1. **Extract `modelStr`** from `body.model` (line 56)
2. **Bypass check** — warmup/naming requests short-circuit before any resolution (line 82)
3. **Combo check first** — `getComboModels(modelStr)` (line 87). If the model string matches a combo name, it enters `handleComboChat` or `handleFusionChat` and **never reaches single-model resolution**.
4. **Capacity adapter augmentation** — `augmentModelsWithCapacityAdapter([modelStr], ...)` (line 120). Can expand a single model into a combo if the request needs capabilities the model lacks.
5. **Single model path** — calls `handleSingleModelChat(body, modelStr, ...)` (line 133)

### Inside `handleSingleModelChat()` (lines 138–310)
1. **`getModelInfo(modelStr)`** — resolves to `{ provider, model }` (line 139)
2. **Null provider = combo fallback** — if `modelInfo.provider === null`, it re-checks combos (lines 142–198). If still null → returns `400 "Invalid model format"` (line 213)
3. **Credential loop** (`while(true)`, line 222):
   - `getProviderCredentials(provider, excludeConnectionIds, model)` (line 223)
   - **⚠️ BLOCKER #1**: If credentials are `null` and `excludeConnectionIds` is empty → returns `404 "No active credentials for provider: ${provider}"` (lines 237–239)
   - Token refresh via `checkAndRefreshToken()` (line 244)
   - Calls `handleChatCore({...})` with resolved credentials (line 268)
   - On failure: `markAccountUnavailable()` → may continue loop or return error

### Where a Virtual Provider Intercepts
The **ideal interception point** is at step 3 (single model path), where `modelStr` like `"modelRouter/auto"` would resolve via `getModelInfo()` to `{ provider: "9router", model: "auto" }`. The existing `NineRouterExecutor` already exists at this position.

---

## 2. `getModelInfo()` Resolution

**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/sse/services/model.js`

### Resolution Order (lines 42–88)
1. **Parse model string** — `parseModel(modelStr)` splits `"provider/model"` into `{ providerAlias, model, isAlias }` (line 43)
2. **Non-alias path** (line 45): Check against `RESERVED_PROVIDER_PREFIXES` (built from registry + local aliases). If not reserved → check user-defined provider nodes (openai-compatible, anthropic-compatible, custom-embedding) by prefix match.
3. **Alias path** (line 72): Check if it's a combo name → return `{ provider: null, model }` to signal combo handling. Otherwise delegate to `getModelInfoCore()`.

### ⚠️ BLOCKER #2: Provider Must Be in Registry
For `"9router/auto"` to resolve to `{ provider: "9router", model: "auto" }`, the string `"9router"` must be in `RESERVED_PROVIDER_PREFIXES`. This set is populated from `REGISTRY` entries (line 13–17). **Currently `9router` is NOT in the provider registry** — grep returned empty on `open-sse/config/providers.js` and `open-sse/providers/registry/*.js`.

Without registry entry: `"9router/auto"` would fall through to provider-node lookup, fail, and return `{ provider: "9router", model: "auto" }` — which actually *works* for the non-alias path since it just passes through the parsed provider string. But the executor dispatch still works because `getExecutor("9router")` has a hardcoded entry.

## 3. `chatCore` → Executor Dispatch

**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js`

### Key Flow (lines 68–350)
1. **Format detection** — `detectFormat(body)` determines source format (line 68)
2. **Target format resolution** — `getModelTargetFormat()`, `resolveTransport()`, `getTargetFormat()` chain (lines 73–77)
3. **Translation** — `translateRequest(sourceFormat, targetFormat, ...)` converts body to upstream format (line 183). Passthrough skips this.
4. **Token savers** — RTK, headroom, caveman, ponytail, pxpipe applied to translated body (lines 250–280)
5. **Executor dispatch** (line 282):
   ```js
   const executor = getExecutor(provider);
   const result = await executor.execute({ model, body: translatedBody, stream, credentials, signal, log, proxyOptions });
   ```
6. **401/403 refresh** — if response is auth error and `!executor.noAuth`, tries token refresh and retries (lines 330–360)

### ⚠️ BLOCKER #3: Credentials Are Passed TO the Executor
`chatCore` receives pre-resolved `credentials` from `handleSingleModelChat`'s credential loop. The executor does **not** resolve its own credentials. For a virtual provider with no real upstream, the credentials object will be whatever `getProviderCredentials("9router")` returns — which is currently **`null`** (no connections configured), causing the `404` at the credential loop level **before chatCore is ever called**.

## 4. Virtual Provider Blockers & Solutions

### Blocker Summary

| # | Blocker | Location | Severity | Solution |
|---|---------|----------|----------|----------|
| 1 | `getProviderCredentials("9router")` returns `null` → 404 | `src/sse/handlers/chat.js:237` | **Critical** | Register as `noAuth` free provider OR add special-case in credential loop |
| 2 | `9router` not in provider registry | `open-sse/providers/registry/` | Medium | Add registry entry with `category: "free"`, `noAuth: true` |
| 3 | Translation runs before executor — body gets mangled | `open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js:183` | Medium | NineRouterExecutor overrides `execute()` entirely, but receives *already-translated* body |
| 4 | `_dispatchToReal()` sets `credentials: null` | `open-sse/executors/9router.js:148` | **Critical** | Real executors need credentials; passing null will fail at their `buildHeaders()` |

### Credential Resolution for Virtual Providers

The **cleanest solution** is the `noAuth` free provider pattern used by `mimo-free`, `ollama-local`, etc.:

In `src/shared/constants/providers.js` line 32: providers with `noAuth: true` in their registry entry get a synthetic credential object:
```js
{ id: "noauth", connectionName: "Public", isActive: true, accessToken: "public", providerSpecificData: { ... } }
```

This bypasses the DB lookup entirely and prevents the 404.

### Can an Executor Call Back Into `handleSingleModelChat`?

**No, not directly.** The `NineRouterExecutor._dispatchToReal()` currently tries to call `realExecutor.execute(dispatchedParams)` directly (line 148), but this **skips**:
- Credential resolution (the real executor needs real credentials)
- Format translation (body was already translated for 9router format)
- Token savers, logging, usage tracking

**Correct callback pattern**: Import and call `handleChatCore` (not `handleSingleModelChat`) with properly resolved credentials for the target provider. Or better: reconstruct a full request and re-enter at `handleSingleModelChat` level via dynamic import:

```js
async _dispatchToReal(provider, model, originalParams, routeTag) {
  // Re-enter the full pipeline so credentials, translation, etc. all run
  const { handleSingleModelChat } = await import("../../sse/handlers/chat.js");
  // But handleSingleModelChat is not exported...
}
```

**⚠️ BLOCKER #6**: `handleSingleModelChat` is **not exported** from `chat.js` (it's a module-private function). Only `handleChat` is exported.

**Working alternative**: The executor can use `handleChatCore` directly, but must resolve credentials itself:
```js
const { getProviderCredentials } = await import("../../sse/services/auth.js");
const creds = await getProviderCredentials(provider);
const result = await handleChatCore({ body, modelInfo: { provider, model }, credentials: creds, ... });
```

## 5. Provider Validation That Rejects No-baseUrl/No-auth

There is **no explicit validation** that rejects providers without a `baseUrl`. The `BaseExecutor.buildUrl()` falls back to empty string, and the fetch would fail at network level. However:

- `getProviderCredentials()` returning `null` is the effective gate (blocks at `chat.js:237`)
- The `noAuth` flag on the executor (`this.noAuth = true`) skips the 401/403 refresh path in `chatCore.js:330`
- No registry validation checks for `baseUrl` presence before allowing requests

## 6. Reference Patterns from Existing Executors

### `perplexity-web.js` — Internal Routing Pattern
- Completely overrides `execute()` — never calls `super.execute()`
- Makes its own HTTP requests to a non-standard endpoint
- Manages its own session cache (FNV-1a hash → backend UUID)
- Parses SSE events manually with `readPplxSseEvents()` generator
- Returns `{ response, url, headers, transformedBody }` matching base contract

### `qoder.js` — Complex Auth + Body Transformation
- Overrides `execute()` entirely
- Has its own credential resolution (`resolveQoderCredentials`)
- Dynamically fetches model configs from upstream API
- Builds completely custom request shape (not OpenAI-compatible)
- Uses COSY signing (RSA + AES + MD5 headers)

### `9router.js` (Existing Skeleton)
- Already overrides `execute()` correctly
- Has the right structure: classify → select → dispatch with fallback
- **Missing**: `smartRouter.js` service, proper credential re-resolution in `_dispatchToReal`, registry entry

## Cross-Cutting Concerns

### FREE_PROVIDERS & Synthetic Credentials

**`src/shared/constants/providers.js`**:
```js
const byCategory = (cat) => Object.fromEntries(
  REGISTRY.filter(r => r.category === cat).map(r => [r.id, buildProviderEntry(r)])
);
export const FREE_PROVIDERS = byCategory("free");
```

✅ **YES** — `FREE_PROVIDERS` is built dynamically from `REGISTRY` filtering by `category === "free"`. Since `9router.js` has `category: "free"` and `noAuth: true`, it **will** appear in `FREE_PROVIDERS` automatically. The `buildProviderEntry()` function explicitly propagates `noAuth: true`.

### Auth Check for Dynamic Providers

**`src/sse/services/auth.js` line 45**:
```js
if (FREE_PROVIDERS[providerId]?.noAuth) {
  // Returns synthetic { id: "noauth", accessToken: "public", ... } connection
}
```

⚠️ **STATIC ONLY** — `FREE_PROVIDERS` is computed **once at module load time** from the static `REGISTRY` array. It will work for `9router` because `9router.js` is statically imported as `p120` in the registry index. However, if a provider were added *dynamically at runtime* (not in the static registry), it would **NOT** get synthetic credentials. For `9router` specifically, this works fine since it's in the static registry.

### Circular Dependency Analysis

This is the **most critical finding**:

```
chatCore.js → imports getExecutor from executors/index.js
executors/index.js → imports NineRouterExecutor from executors/9router.js
executors/9router.js → imports handleChatCore from handlers/chatCore.js  ← CYCLE
```

**The cycle**: `chatCore → executors/index → 9router → chatCore`

However, there are two mitigating factors:
1. **ESM live bindings**: In ESM, circular imports resolve via live bindings. As long as `handleChatCore` is defined before it's *called* (not just imported), it works. Since `handleChatCore` is a function declaration/export in `chatCore.js` and `_dispatchToReal` only calls it at runtime (inside an async method), the binding will be resolved by the time it's invoked.
2. **Dynamic import for auth**: The `getProviderCredentials` import in `_dispatchToReal` uses `await import(...)` which is already safe.

**Verdict**: The circular dependency is **safe at runtime** due to ESM semantics + deferred invocation, but it's architecturally fragile. If `chatCore.js` ever adds top-level side effects that depend on executors being fully initialized, it could break. The dynamic import pattern used for `auth.js` would be safer for `handleChatCore` too.

## Smart Router Architecture Analysis

### The Core Problem
Translation happens inside `handleChatCore()` (line ~178 in `open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js`). By the time an executor runs, the body is already translated to the target provider's format. Re-dispatching to a different-format provider would require reverse-translating, which is lossy and fragile.

**The key insight**: model selection must happen **before** `handleSingleModelChat()` is called, while the body is still in the client's original format.

---

### Option A: Pre-combo Interception in `handleChat()` ✅ RECOMMENDED

**How it works**: Insert a smart-router check at line ~88 of `src/sse/handlers/chat.js`, right after `detectRequiredCapabilities(body)` and before `getComboModels(modelStr)`. If `modelStr` matches a configured smart router name, classify the task from the raw body, select a real model/combo, and replace `modelStr` before any downstream code runs.

```
// Pseudocode insertion point (after line 88):
const requiredCapabilities = detectRequiredCapabilities(body);

// SMART ROUTER CHECK — before combo resolution
if (isSmartRouter(modelStr)) {
  const selectedModel = await classifyAndSelect(body, modelStr, settings);
  if (selectedModel) {
    log.info("SMART", `Router "${modelStr}" → ${selectedModel}`);
    modelStr = selectedModel; // Replace before combo/single-model resolution
  }
}

// Existing combo check continues unchanged...
const comboModels = await getComboModels(modelStr);
```

| Criterion | Assessment |
|-----------|-----------|
| Avoids double-translation? | ✅ **Yes** — model swap happens before any translation. Body stays in client format. |
| Code changes needed | ✅ **Minimal** — ~30 lines in `chat.js` + new classifier module. Zero changes to `chatCore`, translator, or executors. |
| Dashboard integration | ✅ **Natural** — smart routers are just combos with `kind: "smart"`. Existing combo UI shows them. Strategy config via existing `comboStrategies` pattern. |
| Session stickiness | ✅ **Easy** — reuse existing `comboRotationState` Map keyed by combo name, or add a session→model cache keyed by conversation hash. |
| Error fallback | ✅ **Built-in** — if classification fails or selected model errors, fall through to normal combo fallback logic (the replaced `modelStr` can be a combo name itself). |

**Why this wins**: It's architecturally identical to how the capacity adapter already works (lines 140-152 in `chat.js`) — that also swaps/augments models before translation. The smart router is just a more sophisticated version of the same pattern.

## Plan: Smart Router — Pre-Combo Interception (v3)

**TL;DR**: The executor-based approach has a fatal double-translation flaw. The correct architecture is pre-combo interception in `handleChat()` — classify the task and swap the model string *before* any translation happens. This mirrors how the capacity adapter already works.

---

### Critical Finding: Why the Executor Approach Fails

The request flow is:
```
handleChat() → handleSingleModelChat() → handleChatCore() → translateRequest() → executor.execute()
```

By the time `NineRouterExecutor.execute()` runs, `chatCore` has already translated the body to OpenAI format (since 9router's `transport.format` is `"openai"`). When `_dispatchToReal()` tries to re-enter `handleChatCore` for e.g. Anthropic, it passes an **already-translated OpenAI-format body** but with `modelInfo: { provider: "anthropic" }`. `chatCore` would then try to translate from OpenAI → Claude format, but the body is *already* OpenAI — causing either double-translation or format mismatch.

Even passing `originalBody` through doesn't fully solve it: `handleChatCore` detects source format from the body shape via `detectFormat(body)`, not from metadata. If the original body was Claude format and we pass it back with `modelInfo: { provider: "anthropic" }`, it works. But if the client sent OpenAI format and we dispatch to Anthropic, `detectFormat` returns `"openai"` and `chatCore` correctly translates OpenAI → Claude. **However**, the executor has already been called once, logging/usage tracking has already fired for "9router", and re-entering `handleChatCore` creates duplicate logs, double usage tracking, and potential infinite loops if the selected model also resolves to 9router.

**Verdict**: Architecturally fragile. The pre-combo approach avoids all of this.

---

### Correct Architecture: Pre-Combo Interception

Insert smart router resolution at line ~88 of `src/sse/handlers/chat.js`, **after** `detectRequiredCapabilities(body)` and **before** `getComboModels(modelStr)`. This is exactly where the capacity adapter already operates (lines 140-152).

#### Code Block 1: New file `src/sse/services/smartRouter.js`

```js
/**
 * Smart Router — pre-combo task classifier + model selector.
 * Runs BEFORE translation in handleChat(), swapping modelStr
 * to a real model or combo name based on prompt analysis.
 */

import { getSettings } from "@/lib/localDb";
import { PROVIDERS } from "open-sse/config/providers.js";
import {
  DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES,
  MODEL_CAPABILITIES,
} from "open-sse/providers/capabilities.js";
import { matchPattern } from "open-sse/providers/pricing.js";

// ── Task Classification ────────────────────────────────────────

const TASK_RULES = [
  { type: "code:debugging", keywords: ["debug", "fix", "error", "bug", "traceback", "exception"] },
  { type: "code:review", keywords: ["review code", "code review", "audit", "lint"] },
  { type: "code:generation", keywords: ["write", "create", "generate", "implement", "function", "class"], patterns: [/```[\w]*\n/] },
  { type: "agent:multi_step", keywords: ["step by step", "multi-step", "plan and execute"] },
  { type: "math", keywords: ["calculate", "solve", "equation", "math", "formula"] },
  { type: "reasoning", keywords: ["reason", "logic", "deduce", "analyze", "think through"] },
  { type: "research_report", keywords: ["research", "report", "analysis", "investigate"] },
  { type: "creative_writing", keywords: ["story", "poem", "essay", "creative", "fiction"] },
  { type: "summarization", keywords: ["summarize", "summary", "tldr", "brief"] },
  { type: "translation", keywords: ["translate", "translation"] },
];

export function classifyTask(messages) {
  let lastUserContent = "";
  for (let i = messages.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const msg = messages[i];
    if (msg.role === "user") {
      if (typeof msg.content === "string") lastUserContent = msg.content;
      else if (Array.isArray(msg.content)) {
        lastUserContent = msg.content.filter(c => c.type === "text").map(c => String(c.text || "")).join(" ");
      }
      break;
    }
  }
  if (!lastUserContent.trim()) return "general_chat";

  for (const rule of TASK_RULES) {
    if (rule.keywords.some(kw => lastUserContent.toLowerCase().includes(kw.toLowerCase()))) return rule.type;
    if (rule.patterns?.some(p => p.test(lastUserContent))) return rule.type;
  }
  return "general_chat";
}

// ── Model Scoring ──────────────────────────────────────────────

const TASK_WEIGHTS = {
  "code:generation": { tools: 3, reasoning: 2, contextWindow: 2 },
  "code:debugging": { tools: 3, reasoning: 3, contextWindow: 2 },
  "agent:multi_step": { tools: 3, reasoning: 3, contextWindow: 3 },
  math: { reasoning: 3 },
  reasoning: { reasoning: 3, contextWindow: 2 },
  research_report: { reasoning: 2, contextWindow: 3, search: 2 },
  creative_writing: { contextWindow: 2 },
  summarization: { contextWindow: 3 },
  general_chat: { contextWindow: 1 },
};

function resolveCapabilities(modelId) {
  if (MODEL_CAPABILITIES[modelId]) return { ...DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES, ...MODEL_CAPABILITIES[modelId] };
  return { ...DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES };
}

export function scoreModel(provider, modelId, taskType, costQualityTradeoff = 5) {
  const caps = resolveCapabilities(modelId);
  const weights = TASK_WEIGHTS[taskType] || TASK_WEIGHTS.general_chat;
  let score = 0;

  if (weights.tools && caps.tools) score += weights.tools * 10;
  if (weights.reasoning && caps.reasoning) score += weights.reasoning * 10;
  if (weights.search && caps.search) score += weights.search * 10;
  const contextScore = Math.min(caps.contextWindow / 20000, 20);
  score += (weights.contextWindow || 1) * contextScore;

  // Cost heuristic (name-based until real pricing wired in)
  const isExpensive = /opus|pro|max|ultra/i.test(modelId);
  const isCheap = /mini|flash|lite|free|cheap/i.test(modelId);
  if (costQualityTradeoff > 5 && isExpensive) score -= (costQualityTradeoff - 5) * 5;
  if (costQualityTradeoff > 5 && isCheap) score += (costQualityTradeoff - 5) * 3;
  if (costQualityTradeoff < 5 && isExpensive) score += (5 - costQualityTradeoff) * 3;

  return Math.max(0, score);
}

// ── Session Stickiness ─────────────────────────────────────────

const SESSION_TTL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;
const sessionCache = new Map();

function conversationFingerprint(messages) {
  const parts = [];
  for (const msg of messages) {
    if (msg.role === "system" || msg.role === "user") {
      let content = typeof msg.content === "string" ? msg.content :
        Array.isArray(msg.content) ? msg.content.filter(c => c.type === "text").map(c => String(c.text || "")).join(" ") : "";
      parts.push(`${msg.role}:${content.slice(0, 500)}`);
      if (parts.length >= 2) break;
    }
  }
  const str = parts.join("\n");
  let hash = 0x811c9dc5;
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) { hash ^= str.charCodeAt(i); hash = (hash * 0x01000193) >>> 0; }
  return hash.toString(16).padStart(8, "0");
}

export function getStickySession(messages) {
  const fp = conversationFingerprint(messages);
  const entry = sessionCache.get(fp);
  if (!entry || Date.now() - entry.ts > SESSION_TTL_MS) { sessionCache.delete(fp); return null; }
  return entry.modelStr;
}

export function setStickySession(messages, modelStr) {
  const fp = conversationFingerprint(messages);
  sessionCache.set(fp, { modelStr, ts: Date.now() });
  if (sessionCache.size > 500) {
    let oldestKey = null, oldestTs = Infinity;
    for (const [k, v] of sessionCache) { if (v.ts < oldestTs) { oldestTs = v.ts; oldestKey = k; } }
    if (oldestKey) sessionCache.delete(oldestKey);
  }
}

// ── Main Entry Point ───────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Resolve a smart router model string to a real model or combo name.
 * Returns null if not a smart router or no suitable model found.
 */
export async function resolveSmartRouter(modelStr, body, settings) {
  const smartRouterConfig = settings.smartRouter;
  if (!smartRouterConfig?.enabled) return null;

  // Check if this modelStr matches a configured smart router name
  const routerNames = smartRouterConfig.names || ["modelRouter", "auto"];
  if (!routerNames.includes(modelStr)) return null;

  const messages = body.messages || [];

  // 1. Check session stickiness
  const sticky = getStickySession(messages);
  if (sticky) return sticky;

  // 2. Classify task
  const taskType = classifyTask(messages);

  // 3. Score available models from configured providers
  const allowedProviders = smartRouterConfig.allowedProviders || Object.keys(PROVIDERS);
  const costQualityTradeoff = smartRouterConfig.costQualityTradeoff ?? 5;
  const candidates = [];

  for (const providerId of allowedProviders) {
    if (providerId === "9router" || providerId === "9r") continue;
    const providerDef = PROVIDERS[providerId];
    if (!providerDef?.models) continue;
    for (const model of providerDef.models) {
      const modelId = model.id || model;
      const score = scoreModel(providerId, modelId, taskType, costQualityTradeoff);
      candidates.push({ provider: providerId, model: modelId, score, taskType });
    }
  }

  candidates.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);
  if (candidates.length === 0) return null;

  // 4. Build fallback chain: top candidate + next 2 as combo
  const topCandidates = candidates.slice(0, 3);
  const selectedModelStr = `${topCandidates[0].provider}/${topCandidates[0].model}`;

  // Store sticky session
  setStickySession(messages, selectedModelStr);

  return selectedModelStr;
}
```

## Your 4 Requirements → What Exists vs. What Needs Building

### 1. Tiered Fallback Chains (per-model or per-provider)
> *"If I'm using a specific model/provider, I can set fallback models within that provider, or choose the next provider to fall back to in a tier list."*

**What EXISTS:**
- ✅ **Combos** (`/dashboard/combos`) — ordered model lists with sequential fallback. You create a combo like `my-fallback-chain` with `[openai/gpt-4o, anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, deepseek/chat]` and use it as your model string. If model 1 fails with a retryable error (429, 503, 502, 504), it tries model 2, then model 3.
- ✅ **Multi-account fallback** — if you have 3 OpenAI API keys and one gets rate-limited, it automatically rotates to the next.
- ✅ **Capacity Adapter** — global fallback pools per capability (vision, audio). If your chosen model can't handle images, it auto-injects a vision-capable model.

**What's MISSING:**
- ❌ **Per-model fallback config** — there's no UI to say "when `openai/gpt-4o` fails, try `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` next." You have to manually create a combo and use the combo name instead of the model name.
- ❌ **Per-provider fallback chains** — no way to say "if all OpenAI accounts fail, try Anthropic next" as a provider-level setting.
- ❌ **Fallback configuration in the dashboard per-provider/model** — the combo UI exists but isn't connected to individual provider/model settings pages.

**Verdict:** The *engine* is fully built. The *UX for configuring it per-model/per-provider* doesn't exist yet.

---

### 2. Model-Specific Fallback Organization
> *"Research how we can organize this and give me options."*

Here are the architectural options:

| Option | How It Works | Pros | Cons |
|--------|-------------|------|------|
| **A. Combos (existing)** | Create named ordered lists, use combo name as model string | Already works, full fallback engine | Must remember combo names, no per-model attachment |
| **B. Per-model fallback metadata** | Store fallback chain on each model alias in DB (`aliasRepo.js`) | Natural UX: configure fallbacks where you configure models | Requires schema change + new UI |
| **C. Provider-level fallback chains** | Store ordered provider list in settings (`settings.providerFallbackChain`) | Simple global config: "try OpenAI → Anthropic → DeepSeek" | Too coarse — doesn't handle model-specific needs |
| **D. Hybrid: combos + auto-creation** | Smart router creates combos dynamically from scored candidates | Best of both worlds — automatic + uses existing engine | Combos table grows with ephemeral entries |
| **E. Settings-based routing rules** | `settings.routingRules = [{ when: { provider: "openai", error: "429" }, then: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5" }]` | Most flexible, conditional logic | Complex UI, over-engineered for v1 |

**My recommendation:** Start with **Option A + D**. Use existing combos as the runtime mechanism, and build a smart router that *auto-creates* combos from scored candidates. Later add Option B (per-model fallback metadata) as a UX enhancement.

---

### 3. Pseudo/Virtual Model ("modelRouter")
> *"A sudo model that I can choose in any app, and it picks the best model from my configured list. Like Hermes Agent's agiliby or OpenClaw's default model with tool-specific overrides."*

**What EXISTS:**
- ✅ **Capacity Adapter** already does part of this — if your request has images but the target model lacks vision, it auto-injects a vision model. This is exactly the "tool-specific override" pattern you described.
- ✅ **Combo system** — you can already create a combo and use it as a model string in any OpenAI-compatible client.
- ✅ **Task classifier + model scorer** — already written in `open-sse/services/smartRouter.js` (16 task types, capability-weighted scoring, session stickiness).

**What's POSSIBLE with current code:**
- ✅ **Yes, a fake/virtual provider is the right approach.** Register `9router` as a provider with virtual models (`auto`, `best-code`, etc.). To any external app, it looks like just another model. Internally, it classifies the task and dispatches to the best real model.
- ✅ **Vision/tool-specific overrides work today** via the capacity adapter. If you send an image to `9router/auto` and the selected model lacks vision, the capacity adapter will inject a vision-capable fallback.
- ⚠️ **The interception point matters.** As discussed, the executor approach has a double-translation flaw. Pre-combo interception in `handleChat()` is the correct architecture.

**What NEEDS BUILDING:**
- New file: `src/sse/services/smartRouter.js` (app-layer version, imports from open-sse layer)
- ~5 lines added to `src/sse/handlers/chat.js` (pre-combo interception)
- Settings schema for smart router config (enabled, trigger names, allowed providers, cost/quality dial)
- Dashboard UI for configuring the smart router (which models/providers to include, default model, etc.)

---

### 4. Queue-Aware Retry with Concurrency Tracking
> *"Choose models that if they fail, retry in a queue. Be aware of how many agents/calls are using the same model. Low latency."*

**What EXISTS:**
- ✅ **Account-level mutex** — `selectionMutex` in `src/sse/services/auth.js` prevents race conditions during account selection.
- ✅ **Model-level locking** — `isModelLockActive(connection, model)` tracks per-model rate limit locks with exponential backoff.
- ✅ **Rate limit tracking** — `rateLimitedUntil` timestamps per account, `formatRetryAfter()` for proper cooldown.
- ✅ **Transient error cooldown** — `checkFallbackError()` in `open-sse/config/errorConfig.js` classifies errors and applies appropriate wait times (2s × 2^level, max 5 min).

**What's MISSING:**
- ❌ **Global concurrency counter** — no tracking of "how many active requests are hitting `openai/gpt-4o` right now across all clients." The mutex only protects account *selection*, not request counting.
- ❌ **Queue-based retry** — currently retries are immediate (with cooldown). There's no job queue that holds failed requests and replays them when capacity frees up.
- ❌ **Concurrency-aware routing** — the smart router doesn't consider "this model already has 50 active requests, prefer a less-loaded one."

**What's FEASIBLE to build:**
- An in-memory `Map<modelStr, { activeCount, lastFailureTs }>` updated at request start/end in `handleSingleModelChat`. This is lightweight (~O(1) per request) and adds negligible latency.
- Feed `activeCount` into the smart router's scoring function as a load penalty: `score -= activeCount * loadPenaltyWeight`.
- For queue-based retry: more complex. Would need a bounded in-memory queue with TTL. Recommend deferring to Phase 2 — the existing fallback-through-candidates pattern handles most cases without queuing.

/**
 * Smart Router — App-layer pre-combo interception.
 *
 * Runs BEFORE translation in handleChat(). Classifies the task,
 * scores available models, creates/reuses a dynamic combo for
 * automatic error fallback, and tracks concurrency per model.
 *
 * Architecture: pre-combo interception (mirrors capacity adapter pattern).
 * NOT an executor — avoids double-translation flaw.
 */

import { getSettings } from "@/lib/localDb";
import { createCombo, getComboByName, updateCombo } from "@/lib/db/repos/combosRepo.js";
import {
  classifyTask,
  scoreModel,
  getStickySession as _getStickySession,
  setStickySession as _setStickySession,
} from "open-sse/services/smartRouter.js";
import { PROVIDERS } from "open-sse/config/providers.js";
import * as log from "../utils/logger.js";

// ── Concurrency Tracking ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const activeRequests = new Map(); // modelStr → count

export function trackRequestStart(modelStr) {
  activeRequests.set(modelStr, (activeRequests.get(modelStr) || 0) + 1);
}

export function trackRequestEnd(modelStr) {
  const count = (activeRequests.get(modelStr) || 1) - 1;
  if (count <= 0) activeRequests.delete(modelStr);
  else activeRequests.set(modelStr, count);
}

export function getActiveCount(modelStr) {
  return activeRequests.get(modelStr) || 0;
}

// ── Dynamic Combo Management ────────────────────────────────────────────────

const COMBO_PREFIX = "sr-"; // smart router combo prefix
const COMBO_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000; // 30 min before stale combos can be cleaned

/**
 * Get or create a dynamic combo for the given candidates.
 * Returns the combo name to use as modelStr.
 */
async function getOrCreateSmartCombo(candidates, taskType, virtualModel) {
  // Build a stable combo name from the top candidate + task type
  const topModel = candidates[0];
  const safeName = `${COMBO_PREFIX}${virtualModel}-${taskType.replace(/:/g, "-")}`;

  // Check if combo already exists with same models
  const existing = await getComboByName(safeName);
  const candidateModels = candidates.map((c) => `${c.provider}/${c.model}`);

  if (existing) {
    // Update if model list changed
    const existingModels = JSON.parse(existing.models || "[]");
    const modelsMatch =
      existingModels.length === candidateModels.length &&
      existingModels.every((m, i) => m === candidateModels[i]);

    if (!modelsMatch) {
      await updateCombo(existing.id, { models: candidateModels });
      log.info("SMART", `Updated combo "${safeName}" → [${candidateModels.join(", ")}]`);
    }
    return safeName;
  }

  // Create new combo
  try {
    await createCombo({
      name: safeName,
      kind: "llm",
      models: candidateModels,
    });
    log.info("SMART", `Created combo "${safeName}" → [${candidateModels.join(", ")}]`);
  } catch (err) {
    // Race condition: another request created it between our check and create
    if (err.message?.includes("UNIQUE constraint")) {
      return safeName;
    }
    throw err;
  }

  return safeName;
}

// ── Session Stickiness (wraps open-sse version with combo awareness) ────────

function getSticky(messages) {
  return _getStickySession(messages);
}

function setSticky(messages, comboName) {
  _setStickySession(messages, comboName);
}

// ── Main Entry Point ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Resolve a smart router model string to a real combo name.
 * Called from handleChat() BEFORE combo resolution and translation.
 *
 * @param {string} modelStr - The model string from the request
 * @param {object} body - The original request body (untranslated)
 * @param {object} settings - Current settings from DB
 * @returns {Promise<string|null>} Resolved combo name, or null if not a smart router request
 */
export async function resolveSmartRouter(modelStr, body, settings) {
  const config = settings.smartRouter;
  if (!config?.enabled) return null;

  // Check if this modelStr matches a configured trigger name
  const triggerNames = config.names || ["modelRouter"];
  if (!triggerNames.includes(modelStr)) return null;

  const messages = body.messages || [];

  // 1. Check session stickiness first
  const sticky = getSticky(messages);
  if (sticky) {
    log.debug("SMART", `Sticky session hit: ${modelStr} → ${sticky}`);
    return sticky;
  }

  // 2. Classify task from prompt content
  const taskType = classifyTask(messages);

  // 3. Determine allowed providers
  const allowedProviders =
    config.allowedProviders?.length > 0
      ? config.allowedProviders
      : Object.keys(PROVIDERS).filter(
          (id) => id !== "9router" && id !== "9r"
        );

  const costQualityTradeoff = config.costQualityTradeoff ?? 5;
  const maxCandidates = config.maxCandidates ?? 3;

  // 4. Score all candidate models
  const candidates = [];
  for (const providerId of allowedProviders) {
    const providerDef = PROVIDERS[providerId];
    if (!providerDef?.models) continue;

    for (const model of providerDef.models) {
      const modelId = model.id || model;
      let score = scoreModel(providerId, modelId, taskType, costQualityTradeoff);

      // Apply concurrency penalty: prefer less-loaded models
      const fullModelStr = `${providerId}/${modelId}`;
      const activeCount = getActiveCount(fullModelStr);
      if (activeCount > 0) {
        score -= activeCount * 2; // 2 points per active request
      }

      if (score > 0) {
        candidates.push({ provider: providerId, model: modelId, score, taskType });
      }
    }
  }

  // Sort by score descending
  candidates.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);

  if (candidates.length === 0) {
    log.warn("SMART", `No suitable models found for ${modelStr} (task: ${taskType})`);
    return null;
  }

  // 5. Take top N candidates for fallback chain
  const topCandidates = candidates.slice(0, maxCandidates);

  // 6. Create or reuse a dynamic combo with these candidates
  const comboName = await getOrCreateSmartCombo(topCandidates, taskType, modelStr);

  // 7. Store sticky session so subsequent turns use the same combo
  setSticky(messages, comboName);

  log.info(
    "SMART",
    `Router "${modelStr}" → combo "${comboName}" (task: ${taskType}, ` +
      `top: ${topCandidates[0].provider}/${topCandidates[0].model}, ` +
      `candidates: ${topCandidates.length})`
  );

  return comboName;
}
```

### 6. CLI Package Architecture

The CLI (`cli/`) is a **separate npm package** (`9router`) that:
- **Installs** the main app's standalone build into `~/.9router/`
- **Self-heals** SQLite runtime deps (sql.js required, better-sqlite3 optional) into `~/.9router/runtime/node_modules/` at postinstall and runtime
- **Manages** system tray (systray2 on macOS/Linux, PowerShell NotifyIcon on Windows)
- **Launches** the Next.js standalone server via `custom-server.js`
- **Polls** TCP port for readiness instead of fixed waits
- **Supports** subcommands (e.g., `9router xai video`) that bypass the launcher
- **Versions independently** from the root app (both currently at 0.5.50)

Production start:

    → IP extraction from TCP socket
    → h2c upgrade handling
    → Background token refresh scheduler

Docker:
  Multi-stage build → copies standalone + custom-server.js + open-sse + MITM
  ENTRYPOINT: permission fix via su-exec → CMD: node custom-server.js
```

---

## 1. BUILD SYSTEMS

### Package.json Scripts (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/package.json`)

| Script | Command | Purpose |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `dev` | `next dev --port 20127` | Dev server (Turbopack default) |
| `dev:webpack` | `next dev --webpack --port 20127` | Dev server with Webpack |
| `build` | `next build --webpack` | Production build (Webpack forced) |
| `postbuild` | `node scripts/copy-standalone-assets.mjs` | Copies static/public into standalone output |
| `start` | `next start --port 20127` | Standard Next.js production server |
| `dev:bun` | `bun --bun next dev --webpack --port 20127` | Bun runtime dev |
| `build:bun` | `bun --bun next build --webpack` | Bun runtime build |
| `start:bun` | `bun ./.next/standalone/server.js` | Bun standalone (bypasses `next start`) |
| `cli:pack` | `npm --prefix cli run pack:cli` | Build + npm pack CLI |
| `cli:publish` | `npm --prefix cli run publish:cli` | Build + npm publish CLI |

**Key observations:**
- Build **always uses Webpack** (`--webpack` flag), never Turbopack for production
- Dev defaults to Turbopack but has an explicit Webpack fallback
- Output mode is `"standalone"` in `next.config.mjs` — produces a self-contained deployable
- `serverExternalPackages`: `better-sqlite3`, `sql.js`, `node:sqlite`, `bun:sqlite`, `open` — kept external to avoid `import.meta.url` corruption

### Next.js Config (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/next.config.mjs`)

- **Output**: `standalone` (file-traced minimal bundle)
- **Tracing root**: Controlled by `NEXT_TRACING_ROOT_MODE=workspace` for CLI builds (traces hoisted node_modules); defaults to project root for Docker
- **Max body size**: `NINEROUTER_PROXY_CLIENT_MAX_BODY_SIZE` env var, default `128mb`
- **HMR cache**: `serverComponentsHmrCache: true` — caches fetch responses across HMR refreshes
- **Package optimization**: Tree-shakes `@xyflow/react`, `@dnd-kit/*`, `material-symbols`, `marked`
- **Webpack watcher**: Excludes `node_modules`, `.git`, `logs`, `.next`, `gitbook`, `cli`, `tests`, `docs` from file watching
- **Rewrites**: Maps `/v1/*` → `/api/v1/*`, `/codex/*` → `/api/v1/responses`, `/v1beta/*` → `/api/v1beta/*`

### Standalone Asset Copy (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/scripts/copy-standalone-assets.mjs`)

Runs as `postbuild`. Copies two things into `.next/standalone/`:
1. `.next/static/` → `.next/standalone/.next/static/`
2. `public/` → `.next/standalone/public/`

Skips entirely when `NEXT_TRACING_ROOT_MODE=workspace` (CLI build handles its own assets).

### CLI Build (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/cli/scripts/build-cli.js`)

A multi-step build pipeline:
1. **Version sync**: Copies version from `cli/package.json` → root `package.json`
2. **Next.js build**: Runs `npm run build` with `NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-cli-build` and `NEXT_TRACING_ROOT_MODE=workspace`
3. **Copy standalone**: Resolves standalone output (handles nested layouts from Next.js 16), copies to `cli/app/`
4. **Copy custom-server.js**: Injects real-IP wrapper
5. **SQLite drivers**: Bundles `sql.js` + `open` into `cli/app/node_modules/`; **strips `better-sqlite3`** (lives in `~/.9router/runtime` instead)
6. **Static files**: Copies `.next/static` and `public/`
7. **Vendor chunks**: Copies `server/vendor-chunks/`
8. **Server artifacts**: Merges complete `server/` tree (standalone tracing can omit dynamic routes)
9. **Validates**: Asserts `app/api/v1/chat/completions/route.js` and `app/api/v1/messages/route.js` exist

Excludes: `@img`, `sharp`, `detect-libc`, `.env*`, `*.log`, `tmp`, `.DS_Store`

## 3. PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT

### Custom Server (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/custom-server.js`)

Wraps the Next.js standalone HTTP server with three critical behaviors:
1. **Real IP extraction**: Derives client IP from TCP socket (`req.socket.remoteAddress`), strips attacker-controlled `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Real-IP`. Only trusts forwarding headers when TCP peer is loopback (local reverse proxy). Sets `x-9r-real-ip` header for downstream use.
2. **Background token refresh**: Starts OAuth token refresh scheduler on server listen event (imports `src/sse/services/backgroundTokenRefresh.js`). Fail-open if missing (e.g., published CLI without `src/`).
3. **HTTP/2 Cleartext (h2c) downgrade**: Intercepts `upgrade` events for h2c, reads the full request body, then replays through the HTTP/1.1 handler. Handles JetBrains IDE clients that send h2c upgrades.

Entry point: `require("./server.js")` when run directly.

### start.sh (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/start.sh`)
Simple Docker convenience script:
```bash
docker stop 9router && docker rm 9router
docker build -t 9router .
docker run -d --name 9router -p 20128:20128 --env-file .env -v 9router-data:/app/data 9router
```

### Docker Deployment

**Dockerfile** (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/Dockerfile`):
- Multi-stage: `base` → `builder` (Node 22 Alpine + build tools) → `runner` (clean Node 22 Alpine)
- Builder installs deps, runs `npm run build`
- Runner copies: `public/`, `.next/static/`, `.next/standalone/`, `custom-server.js`, `open-sse/`, `src/mitm/`, `node_modules/node-forge`, `node_modules/next`
- Creates `/app/data` and `/app/data-home` directories, symlinks `~/.9router` → `/app/data-home`
- Entrypoint script fixes permissions on mounted volumes via `su-exec`
- CMD: `node custom-server.js`
- Exposes port **20128**

**docker-compose.yml** (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/docker-compose.yml`):
- Two services: `9router` + `headroom` (companion service at port 8787)
- Uses pre-built image `decolua/9router:latest`
- Persistent volume `9router-data` → `/app/data`
- Env: `DATA_DIR=/app/data`, `PORT=20128`, `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0`, `HEADROOM_URL=http://headroom:8787`

### Platform-Specific Configs
- **Vercel**: Deploy route exists at `src/app/api/proxy-pools/vercel-deploy/route.js` — deploys proxy pools to Vercel, not the app itself
- **Fly.io/Railway**: No platform-specific configs found
- **Deno Deploy**: Proxy pool deployment route exists at `src/app/api/proxy-pools/deno-deploy/route.js`
- The app is designed for **self-hosted** deployment (Docker, bare metal, or CLI launcher)

### CLI Launcher (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/cli/cli.js`)
- Published to npm as `9router`
- Binary: `9router` → `cli.js`
- On start: self-heals SQLite runtime + tray runtime, then spawns the bundled Next.js standalone server
- Polls TCP port until server accepts connections (no blind waits)
- Default port: **20128**, host: **0.0.0.0**
- Subcommands like `9router xai video` bypass launcher flow entirely

## 6. PACKAGING FOR DISTRIBUTION

### CLI Pack Flow
```bash
npm run cli:pack   # From repo root
```
Executes: `cli/scripts/build-cli.js` → `npm pack --pack-destination ../..`

### What Goes Into the npm Package (`cli/package.json` `files` field)
- `cli.js` — launcher entry point
- `src/` — CLI source (subcommands)
- `hooks/` — postinstall, sqliteRuntime, trayRuntime
- `app/` — bundled Next.js standalone build (created by build-cli.js)
- `README.md`, `LICENSE`

### Postinstall Hook (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/cli/hooks/postinstall.js`)
Runs on `npm install -g 9router`:
1. **SQLite warm-up**: Installs `better-sqlite3@12.6.2` and `sql.js@1.14.1` into `~/.9router/runtime/node_modules/`
2. **Tray warm-up**: Installs `systray2@2.1.4` on macOS/Linux only (Windows uses PowerShell)
3. Both are **non-fatal** — CLI retries at runtime

### SQLite Runtime Detection (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/cli/hooks/sqliteRuntime.js`)
Priority chain: `bun:sqlite` → `better-sqlite3` (native) → `node:sqlite` (Node ≥22.5) → `sql.js` (pure JS WASM)

- `better-sqlite3` installed to `~/.9router/runtime/node_modules/` (user-writable, avoids Windows EBUSY during global updates)
- Validates native binary magic bytes (ELF/Mach-O/PE) before trusting
- `sql.js` WASM verified in both bundled and runtime locations
- `buildEnvWithRuntime()` injects runtime + bundled paths into `NODE_PATH`

### Tray Runtime (`/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/cli/hooks/trayRuntime.js`)
- Uses `systray2@2.1.4` fork (original `systray@1.0.5` has broken 2017 x86_64 binary)
- Actively removes legacy `systray` from both runtime and global dirs
- Sets executable bit on macOS tray binary (npm sometimes strips it)
- Windows skipped entirely — uses PowerShell `NotifyIcon`

## 1. REQUEST LOGGING & STORAGE

### `requestDetails` Table (Deep Observability)
**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/lib/db/schema.js` (lines 131-148)
**Repo:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/lib/db/repos/requestDetailsRepo.js`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `id` | TEXT PK | Generated: `{ISO-timestamp}-{random6}-{model-slug}` |
| `timestamp` | TEXT NOT NULL | ISO 8601 |
| `provider` | TEXT | Provider ID |
| `model` | TEXT | Model name |
| `connectionId` | TEXT | Account/connection reference |
| `status` | TEXT | "success", "error", etc. |
| `data` | TEXT NOT NULL | **JSON blob** containing the full detail record |

The `data` JSON blob stores (from `flushToDatabase()`, line 97-112):
- `request` — client request body (headers sanitized, truncated to `maxJsonSize`)
- `providerRequest` — translated upstream request body
- `providerResponse` — raw upstream response body
- `response` — final client-facing response (includes `.thinking` if present)
- `latency` — `{ ttft, total }` in ms
- `tokens` — token counts object
- `pxpipe` — image compression metadata if applied
- Sensitive headers (`authorization`, `x-api-key`, `cookie`, `token`, `api-key`) are **stripped** before storage

**Gating:** Controlled by two mechanisms (line 18-35):
1. `ENABLE_REQUEST_LOGS` env var (overrides everything if set)
2. `settings.enableObservability` UI toggle (default: `false`)
3. Fallback: `OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED` env var (default: `true` if no UI flag set)

**Configurable limits** (from settings defaults in `settingsRepo.js` lines 42-46):
- `observabilityMaxRecords`: 1000 (auto-prunes oldest)
- `observabilityBatchSize`: 20 (batch write threshold)
- `observabilityFlushIntervalMs`: 5000
- `observabilityMaxJsonSize`: 5 KB per field (truncates with `_truncated: true` marker)

**⚠️ CRITICAL FINDING: `saveRequestDetail()` is NEVER called in production code.** It is defined and exported but has zero callers in `src/` or `open-sse/`. Only test files mock it. The entire deep request detail capture system is **built but not wired in**.

**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/lib/db/schema.js` (lines 108-128)
**Repo:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/lib/db/repos/usageRepo.js`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| `id` | INTEGER PK AUTO | Auto-increment |
| `timestamp` | TEXT NOT NULL | ISO 8601 |
| `provider` | TEXT | Provider ID |
| `model` | TEXT | Model name |
| `connectionId` | TEXT | Account reference |
| `apiKey` | TEXT | API key used |
| `endpoint` | TEXT | Endpoint path |
| `promptTokens` | INTEGER | Input tokens |
| `completionTokens` | INTEGER | Output tokens |
| `cost` | REAL | Calculated cost |
| `status` | TEXT | "ok", error status |
| `tokens` | TEXT | Full token JSON (includes cached_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens) |
| `meta` | TEXT | Currently always `{}` |

This table is **always written** via `saveRequestUsage()` — no gating. It powers all dashboard analytics.

## 2. USAGE TRACKING

### Metrics Tracked
**File:** `/Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/src/lib/db/repos/usageRepo.js`

Per-request: promptTokens, completionTokens, cachedTokens, cost (calculated via `pricingRepo`), status, provider, model, connectionId, apiKey, endpoint.

### Aggregation (`usageDaily` table)
Pre-aggregated daily buckets stored as JSON in `usageDaily` table. Each day contains:
- Totals: requests, promptTokens, completionTokens, cachedTokens, cost
- Breakdowns: `byProvider`, `byModel`, `byAccount`, `byApiKey`, `byEndpoint`

### Chart Data (`getChartData()`, line 661)
Supports periods: `today` (24 hourly buckets), `24h` (24 hourly buckets rolling), `7d`, `30d`, `60d` (daily buckets). Returns `{ label, tokens, cost }` arrays.

### Live Stats (`getUsageStats()`)
Returns comprehensive stats including:
- Lifetime totals from `_meta.totalRequestsLifetime`
- Per-period breakdowns from `usageDaily`
- Recent requests (last 20 deduped from `usageHistory`)
- Pending requests (in-memory tracking via `trackPendingRequest()`)
- Connection/account name resolution

### In-Memory State
- `pendingRequests` — live count of in-flight requests by model and account
- `recentRing` — ring buffer of last 50 requests for real-time display
- `statsEmitter` — EventEmitter for live dashboard updates (debounced at 150-250ms)
- `lastErrorProvider` — tracks most recent error provider (10s TTL)
