### Data Flow for Message Tracking

```
Client Request (OpenAI/Claude/Gemini format)

handleChat() ──── resolveSmartRouter() ──── [modelStr may change]

handleSingleModelChat() / handleComboChat()
  │                                         ← conversationId resolved here
  │                                           (header / extra_body / hash)

handleChatCore()

  ├── detectFormat(body)                    ← source format identified
  ├── translateRequest()                    ← body translated to target format
  │   ORIGINAL body preserved as `body` param
  │   TRANSLATED body stored as `translatedBody`

  ├── executor.execute({ body: translatedBody, originalBody: body, ... })

  │   ├── SUCCESS: response stream/chunks
  │   └── ERROR: error object with status + body

  ├── [AFTER EXECUTOR RETURNS]
  │   saveRequestDetail({                   ← NEW WIRING POINT
  │     request: sanitizedClientBody,       ← original, headers stripped
  │     providerRequest: translatedBody,    ← what was sent upstream
  │     providerResponse: rawUpstreamResp,  ← what came back
  │     response: finalClientResponse,      ← what client received
  │     latency: { ttft, total },
  │     tokens: { prompt, completion, cached },
  │     conversationId: resolvedId,         ← NEW FIELD
  │     errorBody: error?.body,             ← NEW FIELD
  │     logLevel: currentLogLevel,          ← NEW FIELD
  │     fallbackChain: [...],              ← NEW FIELD (from combo)

  └── Return response to client

  ⚠️ ORIGINAL MESSAGE BODY IS NEVER MODIFIED
  - Client request passes through unchanged
  - Only captured/stored copies are sanitized
  - Translation creates a NEW object, doesn't mutate original
  - Smart router changes modelStr (routing metadata), not message content
```

### Log Levels Design

| Level | What Gets Stored | Use Case |
|-------|-----------------|----------|
| `debug` | Full request + response bodies, all headers (sanitized), thinking blocks, PXPIPE stats, tool calls | Development, debugging specific issues |
| `info` | Request summary (model, tokens, latency, status), truncated bodies (first 500 chars), error messages | Default production level, general monitoring |
| `warn` | Only requests with warnings or partial failures, error bodies, fallback chain events | Monitoring degraded service |
| `error` | Only failed requests with full error context | Alerting, incident response |

Controlled by `settings.observabilityLogLevel` (default: `"info"`). Can be overridden per-request via `extra_body.log_level` header.

### Dynamic Filter System Design

```
Filter State = {
  providers: string[],        // multi-select from active providers
  models: string[],           // multi-select, filtered by selected providers
  status: string[],           // ["success", "error", "timeout", "rate_limited"]
  errorCategories: string[],  // ["auth", "rate_limit", "overloaded", "content_filter", "timeout"]
  conversationId: string,     // exact match or search
  dateRange: { start, end },  // date picker
  minTokens: number,          // slider
  maxLatency: number,         // slider
  searchText: string,         // full-text search across request/response bodies
  taskType: string[],         // from smart router classification (if available)
}

Saved Presets = settings.filterPresets[] = {
  name: "Production Errors Last 24h",
  filters: { status: ["error"], dateRange: "24h" }
}
```

Filters apply server-side via SQL WHERE clauses on `usageHistory` + `requestDetails` JOIN. Results paginated (50/page). Filter state persisted in URL params for shareable links.

## Fallback System: What Exists vs What's Missing

### Currently Working ✅

| Capability | Mechanism | How to Use |

| **Multi-account rotation** | Credential loop in `handleSingleModelChat()` | Automatic when multiple API keys configured for same provider |
| **Capability-based auto-switch** | Capacity Adapter (`/dashboard/combos` bottom section) | Enable vision/audio adapter, add fallback models per capability |
| **Transient error retry** | `checkFallbackError()` in combo handler | Automatic — retries on 429/502/503/504 with cooldown |
| **Token refresh retry** | `checkAndRefreshToken()` in credential loop | Automatic on 401 for OAuth providers |
| **Round-robin load balancing** | Per-combo strategy setting | Set combo strategy to "round-robin" |
| **Fusion (parallel + judge)** | Per-combo strategy setting | Set combo strategy to "fusion", pick judge model |

### Smart Router Adds (Implemented, Not Yet Enabled) ✅

| Capability | Mechanism | Status |
|-----------|-----------|--------|
| **Task-aware model selection** | Pre-combo interception classifies prompt → scores models | Code complete, needs `smartRouter.enabled=true` |
| **Dynamic fallback chains** | Auto-creates combos from top N scored candidates | Code complete |
| **Concurrency-aware routing** | Penalizes heavily-loaded models in scoring | Code complete |
| **Session stickiness** | 5-min TTL conversation fingerprint → same model chain | Code complete |

| **Per-provider fallback chains** | Can't say "if all OpenAI accounts fail, try Anthropic" as a provider-level setting | Medium — new settings structure |

| **Model-to-provider cross-routing** | Can't configure "model A on provider X → fallback to any model on provider Y" | Medium — extends combo system |

### Relationship Between Systems

```
User sends request with model="modelRouter"

Smart Router (pre-combo interception)
  ├── Classifies task type
  ├── Scores all available models
  ├── Creates/updates dynamic combo: sr-modelRouter-code-generation
  │     Models: [openai/gpt-4o, anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, deepseek/chat]
  └── Returns combo name as new modelStr

Existing Combo Engine (handleComboChat)
  ├── Tries openai/gpt-4o first
  │   ├── Success → return response ✅
  │   └── 429/503 → wait cooldown, try next
  ├── Tries anthropic/claude-sonnet-5
  │   ├── Success → return response ✅
  │   └── Error → try next
  └── Tries deepseek/chat
      ├── Success → return response ✅
      └── Error → return 503 with last error

Capacity Adapter (runs INSIDE each model attempt)
  └── If request has images but model lacks vision → inject vision-capable fallback
```

The smart router **selects** the best candidates. The combo engine **executes** the fallback chain. The capacity adapter **augments** each individual attempt. These three layers compose cleanly.

      status: "error"
    })).catch(() => {});

    return {
      success: false,
      response: new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: { message: `[${status}]: ${shortMsg}` } }), {
        status,
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*' },
      }),
    };
```

## 1. SETTINGS API

**Route:** `src/app/api/settings/route.js` — exists with `GET` and `PATCH` (no `PUT`).

**GET** (returns merged settings + env flags, secrets stripped.

**GET**  :
```js
export async function GET() {
  const settings = await getSettings();
  const { password, oidcClientSecret, ...safeSettings } = settings;
  safeSettings.oidcConfigured = !!(safeSettings.oidcIssuerUrl && safeSettings.oidcClientId && oidcClientSecret);
  return NextResponse.json({ ...safeSettings, enableRequestLogs, enableTranslator, hasPassword: !!password }, ...);
}
```

**PATCH** (partial update — this is what pages call):
```js
export async function PATCH(request) {
  const body = await request.json();
  for (const key of PROTECTED_SETTING_KEYS) delete body[key];  // ["password", "mitmSudoEncrypted"]
  // ... password hashing, oidc secret handling ...
  const settings = await updateSettings(body);
  // side effects: applyOutboundProxyEnv, resetComboRotation (on comboStrategy/comboStrategies change),
  //                configureQuotaAutoPing (on claudeAutoPing/codexAutoPing)
  return NextResponse.json(safeSettings, ...);
}
```

**How pages call it** (from `combos/page.js`):
```js
// read — parallel fetch with other data
const [combosRes, providersRes, settingsRes] = await Promise.all([
  fetch("/api/combos"), fetch("/api/providers"), fetch("/api/settings"),
]);
const settingsData = settingsRes.ok ? await settingsRes.json() : {};
setCapacityAdapter(normalize(settingsData.capacityAdapter));

// write
await fetch("/api/settings", {
  method: "PATCH",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ capacityAdapter: next }),
});
```

**Repo** (`src/lib/db/repos/settingsRepo.js`):
```js
export async function getSettings()          // readRaw() + mergeWithDefaults(raw)
export async function updateSettings(updates) // atomic read-merge-write in a transaction (upsert row id=1)
```
- Stored as one JSON blob in `settings(id=1, data)`; `updateSettings` does shallow `{ ...current, ...updates }` — so **nested objects like `smartRouter` must be replaced whole** (PATCH the full `smartRouter` object, not individual keys).
- `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` already includes:
```js
smartRouter: {
  enabled: false,
  names: ["modelRouter"],
  allowedProviders: [],
  costQualityTradeoff: 5,
  maxCandidates: 3,
},
```

## 2. COMBOS PAGE STRUCTURE

**File:** `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/combos/page.js` (`"use client"`, ~900 lines — larger than the ~650 estimate).

**State pattern:** plain `useState`/`useEffect` + `fetch`, no SWR/React Query:
- `fetchData()` — `Promise.all` of `/api/combos`, `/api/providers`, `/api/settings`; runs once in `useEffect(..., [])`
- Settings saves are **optimistic** (setState first, then PATCH; error just console.logs)

**Components (all in the same file):**

| Component | Props | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `CombosPage` (default) | — | State owner: `combos, loading, showCreateModal, editingCombo, activeProviders, comboStrategies, capacityAdapter, confirmState` |
| `ComboCard` | `{ combo, getCaps, activeProviders, copied, onCopy, onEdit, onDelete, strategy, onSetStrategy }` | List row; strategy `Select` + copy/edit/delete buttons + fusion judge picker |
| `CapacityAdapterSection` | `{ capacityAdapter, onChange, activeProviders, getCaps }` | **The settings-editing section to mirror** — header w/ explanation + list of cap cards |
| `CapacityAdapterCap` | `{ cap, entry, onChange, activeProviders, getCaps }` | Per-capability card: master `Toggle`, model chips with move-up/down/remove, round-robin `Toggle`, "Add Model" button → `ModelSelectModal` |
| `ModelItem` | `{ id, index, model, isFirst, isLast, onEdit, onMoveUp, onMoveDown, onRemove }` | Drag-sortable inline-edit row (`@dnd-kit`) |
| `ComboFormModal` | `{ isOpen, combo, onClose, onSave, activeProviders, kindFilter }` | Create/edit modal (`Input` name + dnd model list + `ModelSelectModal`) |

**Capacity adapter save path (the exact pattern to copy):**
```js
const handleSetCapacityAdapter = async (next) => {
  setCapacityAdapter(next);                    // optimistic
  await fetch("/api/settings", { method: "PATCH", ... body: JSON.stringify({ capacityAdapter: next }) });
};
```
- `CapacityAdapterSection` renders `CAPACITY_ADAPTER_CAPS` (`[{key:"vision",...},{key:"audioInput",...}]`), each `CapacityAdapterCap` patches via `onChange({ ...capacityAdapter, [cap.key]: entry })` (whole-object replace, matching the shallow-merge repo).
- Normalization helpers exist for backward compat: `normalizeCapEntry(entry)` (array→object) and `EMPTY_CAPACITY_ADAPTER`.
- Delete uses a `ConfirmModal` via `confirmState` (`{title, message, onConfirm}`).
- Icons: Material Symbols (`<span className="material-symbols-outlined">…</span>`).

**A Smart Router section would slot in as a sibling of `CapacityAdapterSection`** inside the page's return, with its own `handleSetSmartRouter(next)` → `PATCH /api/settings { smartRouter: next }`, reading `settingsData.smartRouter` in `fetchData()`.

## 5. USAGE TRACKING

**`saveUsageStats`** lives in `open-sse/handlers/chatCore/requestDetail.js` (not `chatCore/` as a folder at the top level — it's `open-sse/handlers/chatCore/requestDetail.js`):

```js
export function saveUsageStats({ provider, model, tokens, connectionId, apiKey, endpoint, label = "USAGE", silent = false, conversationId }) {
  // skips if 0 tokens; logs 📊 line
  const normalized = canonicalizeUsage(tokens) || {...};
  saveRequestUsage({
    provider, model, tokens: normalized,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    connectionId, apiKey, endpoint: endpoint || null,
    conversationId: conversationId || undefined
  }).catch(() => {});
}
```

**Callers** (all pass `conversationId` through):
- `open-sse/handlers/chatCore/nonStreamingHandler.js:321`
- `open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingHandler.js:158`
- `open-sse/handlers/chatCore/sseToJsonHandler.js:208, 308`

**Flow:**
`src/sse/handlers/chat.js:270-283` resolves `conversationId` (`x-conversation-id` header → `body.extra_body.conversation_id` → null) → passed to `handleChatCore({ ..., conversationId })` → placed in `sharedCtx` (`chatCore.js:429`) → handlers call `saveUsageStats`/`buildRequestDetail({ ..., conversationId })` → `saveRequestDetail` (buffered, flush on batch size/timer — `requestDetailsRepo.js`) and `saveRequestUsage` (immediate transactional).

**`saveRequestUsage(entry)`** — `src/lib/db/repos/usageRepo.js:241`. Accepted fields (from destructuring/INSERT):
```js
{ timestamp, provider, model, connectionId, apiKey, endpoint,
  promptTokens, completionTokens, cost, status, tokens, meta, conversationId }
```
- Dedup check on (timestamp, provider, model, connectionId, apiKey, promptTokens, completionTokens)
- Single transaction: insert into `usageHistory` (with `conversationId` column, indexed — `schema.js:124,131`) → upsert `usageDaily` aggregate → bump `_meta.totalRequestsLifetime`
- **There is NO `taskType` field.** The only unused slot is `meta` (always `stringifyJson({})` — a free-form JSON blob already in the schema, never written to). `classifyTask()` in `open-sse/services/smartRouter.js` produces a taskType but it's not persisted anywhere.
- Note: `saveRequestUsage` is also called from `src/sse/handlers/embeddings.js:140` (without conversationId).

## 6. SMART ROUTER CURRENT STATE

**File:** `src/sse/services/smartRouter.js` (app-layer; also `open-sse/services/smartRouter.js` holds pure `classifyTask`/`scoreModel`/`getStickySession`).

```js
export async function resolveSmartRouter(modelStr, body, settings)
// @returns Promise<string|null> — resolved combo name, or null if not a smart router request
```

Reads settings keys:
- `settings.smartRouter.enabled` (false → early return null)
- `settings.smartRouter.names` (default `["modelRouter"]` — modelStr must match a trigger name)
- `settings.smartRouter.allowedProviders` (empty → all `PROVIDERS` except `9router`/`9r`)
- `settings.smartRouter.costQualityTradeoff` (default 5, passed to `scoreModel`)
- `settings.smartRouter.maxCandidates` (default 3, top-N fallback chain)

Dynamic combo naming:
```js
const COMBO_PREFIX = "sr-";                 // smart router combo prefix
const COMBO_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;        // 30 min stale-combo cleanup window
const safeName = `${COMBO_PREFIX}${virtualModel}-${taskType.replace(/:/g, "-")}`;
```
So a request to model `modelRouter` classified as `code:debug` creates/updates combo `sr-modelRouter-code-debug` (kind `"llm"`, models = `["provider/model", ...]` from `getOrCreateSmartCombo`), with UNIQUE-constraint race handling. Flow: sticky session check → `classifyTask(messages)` → score all provider models → concurrency penalty (2 pts per active request via in-memory `activeRequests` Map) → top-N → create/update combo → `setSticky`. Wired in `src/sse/handlers/chat.js:91-93` **before** combo resolution/translation: `const smartRouterResult = await resolveSmartRouter(modelStr, body, settings); if (smartRouterResult) modelStr = smartRouterResult;`

## 1. Your 4-5 Things — What They Are, What Code Changed, Where in the UI

### Thing 1: Smart Router (virtual "modelRouter" model) ✅ NOW WORKING
**What:** Use `modelRouter` (or any name you configure) as your model string in *any* app. 9router classifies the task, scores all your providers' models, builds an automatic fallback combo, and retries down the list if one fails.

**Code:** `9f4c1631` (interception), `acdc7134` (UI), `1c921ce2` (metrics), **`4627a299` (4 real bugs fixed — see below)**
**Where in UI:** `/dashboard/combos` → **Smart Router card** (enable toggle, trigger names, allowed providers, cost/quality slider, fallback chain size)

### Thing 2: Tiered Fallback (per-model/per-provider chains) ✅ Working
**What:** Combos = ordered model lists with Fallback/Round-Robin/Fusion strategies. I added **fallback chain visibility** — you now see *which* models were tried and why.
**Code:** `5932879f` (fallback chain logging)
**Where in UI:** `/dashboard/combos` → **Create Combo** (this existed before; my addition makes each attempt visible in responses/logs)

### Thing 3: Per-Conversation Logging + Export ✅ Working
**What:** Every request captures conversationId, request/response bodies, latency, tokens, error categories. Filterable per conversation, exportable as JSON or **markdown**, and auto-flushed to disk daily.
**Code:** `6f00d23f`, `a954b88f`, `d9415807`, `57e87729`, `3e7d1c7c`, `40168739`
**Where in UI:** `/dashboard/usage?tab=details` → Conversation ID filter + Conversation column + detail drawer. `/dashboard/combos` → **Markdown Request Log** card. Files at `~/.9router/logs/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. **Proven:** mock 429 upstream → captured with `conversationId` + `errorCategory: "rate_limit"`, markdown file written.

### Thing 4: AI Error Analyst ✅ Working
**What:** In the request detail drawer, click **"Analyze error with AI"** on any failed request — it sends the captured context to a model of your choice (`settings.analyzeErrorModel`, default `oc/mimo-v2.5-free`) and returns a diagnosis.
**Code:** `d1c1db28`
**Where in UI:** `/dashboard/usage?tab=details` → Detail → **AI Error Analysis** panel on error rows

### Thing 5: Error Categorization ✅ Working

Research complete. Here is the full trace of the model-selection data flow.

---

## 1. `ModelSelectModal` — how it builds the list (`src/shared/components/ModelSelectModal.js`)

**It does NOT call `/api/providers` or `/api/models`.** The provider list comes entirely from the `activeProviders` **prop** (line 26, `activeProviders = []`). It only fetches auxiliary data while open:

| Fetch | Line | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/providers/${connectionId}/models` | 63–99 | Live per-account catalog, **cursor connections only** |
| `/api/combos` | 101–114 | Combo section at top of the modal |
| `/api/provider-nodes` | 116–130 | Display names/prefixes for compatible providers |
| `/api/models/custom` | 132–147 | User-added custom models |
| `/api/models/disabled` | 149–162 | Disabled-model filter |

The gating logic is in the `groupedModels` memo (line ~197–208):

```js
// Get all active provider IDs from connections (filtered by kindFilter if set)
const activeConnectionIds = filteredActiveProviders.map(p => p.provider);

// No-auth providers: filter by kindFilter as well
const noAuthIds = kindFilter
  ? NO_AUTH_PROVIDER_IDS.filter(...)
  : NO_AUTH_PROVIDER_IDS;

// Only show connected providers (including both standard and custom)
const providerIdsToShow = new Set([
  ...activeConnectionIds,  // Only connected providers
  ...noAuthIds,            // No-auth providers (kind-filtered)
]);
```

So the visible set = **connected providers + no-auth free providers** (`NO_AUTH_PROVIDER_IDS` is defined at line 18–19 as `Object.keys(FREE_PROVIDERS).filter(id => FREE_PROVIDERS[id].noAuth)`).

- **Grouping**: grouped **by provider** — each group gets a `ProviderIcon`, name, and model count (`{providerId}` header), rendered at lines 542–603. Not flat, not by type.
- **Model source per provider**: `getModelsByProviderId(providerId)` (imported line 9), which resolves the provider's alias and returns `PROVIDER_MODELS[alias]` from the static catalog (defined in `open-sse/config/providerModels.js` lines 108–113). So the *catalog* is full — but it's only queried **for providers that made it into `providerIdsToShow`**.
- **Search**: `filteredGroups` (lines 429–460) — case-insensitive substring match on provider name OR model `name`/`id`. Combos filtered by name separately (lines 396–403).
- **Sorting**: alphabetically, with already-added models floated to top (`sortModels`, lines 405–412).

## 2. Where `activeProviders` comes from (combos page)

`src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/combos/page.js`:

- Line 52: `const [activeProviders, setActiveProviders] = useState([]);`
- Lines 75–79 in `fetchData`:
```js
const providersRes = await fetch("/api/providers");
...
if (providersRes.ok) {
  setActiveProviders(providersData.connections || []);
}
```

So `activeProviders` = **`GET /api/providers` → `connections`** — i.e. **only CONNECTED providers that have credential rows**. It is passed down unchanged: `ComboFormModal activeProviders={activeProviders}` (lines 309–326) → `<ModelSelectModal activeProviders={activeProviders} ...>` (line 1046). Note the combos page defines its **own local `ComboFormModal`** at line 859 (not the shared `src/shared/components/ComboFormModal.js`), but it passes the same prop. **This is the root cause**: only providers with connections ever render in the picker.

## 3–4. What the API routes return

**`src/app/api/providers/route.js` GET (lines 50–77)** — **connections only**:
```js
const connections = await getProviderConnections();
...
return NextResponse.json({ connections: safeConnections });
```
No registry, no model catalog. (Secrets stripped; `name` enriched for compatible nodes.)

**`src/app/api/v1/models/route.js`** (the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/models`) — **connection-gated too**, but interestingly:
- Lines 250–260: `connections = await getProviderConnections()` filtered by `isActive !== false`.
- Line 288–291: `activeConnectionByProvider` map.
- **Lines 312–313: `if (connections.length === 0)`** → only then does it iterate the **full static `PROVIDER_MODELS` catalog** ("DB unavailable → return static models").
- Lines 330+: with connections present, it iterates **only `activeConnectionByProvider`** — one group per connected provider, merging static models, live resolvers (kiro/qoder/github/cursor…), custom models, and aliases.

**The one full-catalog dashboard endpoint is `src/app/api/models/route.js` GET (lines 11–42)**: it returns **`AI_MODELS`** — the entire static catalog built in `src/shared/constants/models.js` line 33–35:
```js
export const AI_MODELS = Object.entries(MODELS).flatMap(([alias, models]) =>
  models.map(m => ({ provider: alias, model: m.id, name: m.name }))
);
```
…enriched per model with `fullModel`, `routedModel`, `alias`, and `caps` — **all 40+ providers, regardless of connection state**. The dashboard already consumes it: `useModelCaps` (`src/shared/hooks/useModelCaps.js` lines 22–31) fetches `/api/models` to get capability badges. So the full catalog data is already in the browser on every page that renders `CapacityBadges` — just never used to populate the selector.

## 5. The model catalog concept

Yes: `PROVIDER_MODELS` in `open-sse/providers/index.js` (lines 40–50) is built from the registry, keyed by `entry.alias || entry.id`:
```js
if (entry.models !== undefined) PROVIDER_MODELS[entry.alias || entry.id] = entry.models.map(normalizeModel);
```
Re-exported via `open-sse/config/providerModels.js` (`export { PROVIDER_MODELS }`) and `src/shared/constants/models.js`. API routes that import it directly:
- `src/app/api/v1/models/route.js` (line 1)
- `src/app/api/v1/models/info/route.js` (line 1 — metadata for a single `alias/modelId`, full catalog lookup)
- `src/app/api/v1beta/models/route.js` and `[...path]/route.js`
- `src/app/api/providers/[id]/models/route.js` (line 129, per-connection config)
- `src/sse/services/smartRouter.js` (line 21)

The dashboard-callable full-catalog surface is **`GET /api/models`** (and per-model `GET /v1/models/info`).

## 6. What the combos page actually passes

From `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/combos/page.js` line 1040–1057 (local `ComboFormModal`):
```js

  isOpen={showModelSelect}

- Other usages on the page: judge-model picker (lines 448–461, **no `modelAliases` passed**) and the capacity-adapter picker (lines 591–600, `capFilter={cap.key}`).

## 7. Filters and empty state

- **`kindFilter`** (lines 37–46, 176–186): filters providers by `AI_PROVIDERS[p].serviceKinds` and models by kind (`llm` default — models with `kind`/`type` other than `llm` are hidden unless `isPlaceholder`/`isCustom`). `TYPED_KINDS` = image/tts/stt/embedding/imageToText; `webSearch`/`webFetch` are provider-as-model.
- **`capFilter`** (lines 432–437): `models.filter((m) => getCaps(m.value)?.[capFilter] === true)` — vision/audioInput etc. via `useModelCaps` (which itself loads the **full** catalog from `/api/models`).
- **Empty state** (lines 596–603):
```jsx
{Object.keys(filteredGroups).length === 0 && filteredCombos.length === 0 && (
  <div className="text-center py-4 text-text-muted">
    <span className="material-symbols-outlined text-2xl mb-1 block">search_off</span>
    <p className="text-xs">No models found</p>
  </div>
)}
```

## What the user sees with only one connected provider

On a fresh install (say, only a no-auth/free test provider connected, no combos):
1. Combos page → **Create Combo → Add Model** opens "Add Model to Combo".
2. The **Combos** section is absent (no combos).
3. Exactly **one provider group** renders (the connected one) with its hardcoded models from `getModelsByProviderId` — e.g. a single "MiMo Auto"-style entry. (No-auth free providers like `mimo-free`, `open-sse/providers/registry/mimo-free.js` — `noAuth: true`, `hidden: true` — also leak into the list via `NO_AUTH_PROVIDER_IDS`, since neither `byCategory` in `providers.js` nor the modal filters `hidden`.)
4. The other 40+ providers (claude, openai, gemini, kiro…) are **invisible** — their static catalogs exist in `PROVIDER_MODELS` but are never queried because they never enter `providerIdsToShow`.
5. If no providers at all matched: the `search_off` / "No models found" empty state.

This matches the report: the modal shows "providers and model types" only in the sense that it shows *provider groups* for *connected* providers — never the full model catalog.

## The minimal fix to show ALL registered models

**Option A — one-line change in `ModelSelectModal.js` (line ~204–208)** — include the entire registry instead of only connections:
```js
const providerIdsToShow = new Set([
  ...Object.keys(AI_PROVIDERS).filter((id) => !AI_PROVIDERS[id]?.hidden),
  ...activeConnectionIds,
]);
```
The existing grouping code already handles every branch (passthrough/alias models, custom-compatible providers, hardcoded `getModelsByProviderId`), so every provider with models would render; groups with zero models are naturally skipped (e.g. line 309 `if (combined.length > 0)`, line 385 `if (allModels.length > 0)`).

**Option B — data-driven, no prop surgery**: have `ModelSelectModal` fetch `GET /api/models` (it already returns `{ provider, model, name, fullModel, routedModel, alias, caps }` for **all** providers) and build groups from `routedModel` values — the same data `useModelCaps` already pulls, so no new endpoint or server work is needed. This is also the only route that keeps the selector correct for providers whose `models` differ from the hardcoded registry (compatible nodes, live resolvers).

For consistency, `src/app/api/v1/models/route.js` has the same connection-gating (full static list only when `connections.length === 0`), so if the goal is "all models always routable/listed," the same change would apply there (lines 312–313 fallback branch).

## Your Questions, Answered

### 1. "Are combos related to a combo being a model itself?"
**Yes — exactly.** A combo's **name becomes a model string**. Create a combo named `my-chain`, and any client can send `{"model": "my-chain"}` — 9Router treats it as a virtual model that tries each model in order. That's the core idea: combos ARE virtual models with built-in fallback.

### 2. "How does the smart router work?"
`modelRouter` is a **virtual model** you can use in any app. When a request hits it:
1. Classify the task (code, math, chat…) from the prompt
2. Score **all your providers' models** by capability fit + cost/quality setting
3. Auto-create a combo with the top 3 (e.g. `sr-modelRouter-code-generation`)
4. Try them in order — if one fails, the next is tried automatically
5. Remember the choice for 5 min per conversation (stickiness)

### 3. "Why do I only see mock providers when adding models?" — **REAL BUG, NOW FIXED** ✅
The model picker only showed **connected** providers — you had only the mock connected, so that's all you saw. The full catalog of 40+ providers existed but was never shown.

**Fix (commit `99ac899f`):** the picker now shows the **entire 9Router catalog** — every provider's models, connected or not — with an amber **"not connected"** badge so you know which need credentials first. This applies to combos, vision/audio adapter, and judge pickers. **Verified live**: Claude, OpenAI, etc. now appear in the modal.

### 4. "Can I choose a specific subset of models for the smart router?" — **NOW BUILT** ✅
New **"Allowed models"** field in the Smart Router card. You can restrict it to exact models or wildcards:
- `openai/gpt-4o` — just that model
- `anthropic/claude-*` — any claude model from Anthropic
- `*/*-thinking` — any thinking model from any provider

### 5. "Can I set fallback models directly on a model/provider?" — **NOW BUILT** ✅
New **"Per-Model / Per-Provider Fallbacks"** card on the combos page (kept alongside combos, as you suggested). One rule per line:
```
openai/gpt-4o:anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6,deepseek/chat
anthropic:deepseek/chat
```
**Proven live**: I set `mock429/gpt-4o-mini → openai/gpt-4o, deepseek/chat` through the UI, sent a request, and the server log shows it tried all 3 in order: `Model fallback "mock429/gpt-4o-mini" → [mock429/gpt-4o-mini → openai/gpt-4o → deepseek/chat]` — falling through on each failure, with the full `fallbackChain` in the response.

### What Actually Controls Chat Continuation

Chat stopping is typically caused by:
1. **Model output token limits** — the model hits its max output tokens mid-response
2. **Network timeouts** — long responses get cut off
3. **Copilot Chat extension bugs** — known issues with response streaming
4. **Rate limiting** — hitting API rate limits mid-stream

Since this isn't a workspace settings issue, the relevant things to investigate are:

All three paths verified: single stream = 1 `[DONE]`, combo stream = 1 `[DONE]`, non-stream = clean JSON. Now I'll update all tracking docs and make detailed, well-attributed commits.

SSE Duplicate Leak Investigation\n\n**Date:** 2026-08-06\n**Author:** GitHub Copilot agent (main session)\n**Status:** resolved\n**Tags:** bug, streaming, sse, passthrough, done-leak\n\n---\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nWhen streaming through 9Router (both single-model and combo), the SSE stream sent `data: [DONE]` **twice** to the client. This violates the OpenAI SSE protocol and could confuse downstream clients that parse the `[DONE]` sentinel as a stream terminator.\n\n**First observed:** During E2E testing of the combo streaming path with mock upstream on port 24000.\n\n---\n\n## Investigation Timeline\n\n### Step 1: Reproduce with mock upstream\n- Mock upstream (`/tmp/mock-upstream.cjs`) sends exactly **one** `data: [DONE]\\n\\n` at stream end\n- Verified by `curl` directly to port 24000 — confirmed single `[DONE]`\n\n### Step 2: Test through 9Router (port 20130)\n- Single modelstreaming: **2 `[DONE]`** (bug confirmed)
- Combo streaming: **2 `[DONE]`** (bug confirmed)
- Non-streaming combo: clean JSON (no leak)

### Step 3: Isolate the source
- Searched entire codebase for literal `[DONE]` strings — not found in open-sse/
- Found `streamDoneSent` flag in `open-sse/utils/stream.js` line ~80 — tracks duplicate prevention
- Read passthrough `transform()` logic (lines 105-210): when upstream sends `data: [DONE]`, the condition `trimmed.slice(5).trim() !== "[DONE]"` **skips** the JSON parse block, falls through to the generic forwarder which emits the line but **never sets `streamDoneSent = true`**
- Read `flush()` logic (lines 370-400): `if (!streamDoneSent && !isGeminiFamily)` adds a second `[DONE]`

### Root Cause
In `STREAM_MODE.PASSTHROUGH`, the `[DONE]` sentinel passes through `transform()` via the fallback path (not the JSON-parse path), so `streamDoneSent` is never set. Then `flush()` unconditionally adds another one.

**This is NOT combo-specific** — it affects ALL passthrough streaming (single model + combo). The bug was introduced when passthrough mode was added without updating the `[DONE]` tracking that already existed for translate mode.

---

## Fix Applied

**File:** `open-sse/utils/stream.js`
**Location:** After line ~200, inside the passthrough `transform()` block, after the output is enqueued

```javascript
// Track [DONE] sentinel to prevent duplicate emission in flush().
// Upstream already sent the terminator — don't re-emit on stream end.
if (trimmed === "data: [DONE]") {
  streamDoneSent = true;
}
```

**Why this works:** When the upstream's `[DONE]` line passes through the passthrough forwarder, we now mark it as sent. When `flush()` runs at stream end, the guard `!streamDoneSent` prevents the duplicate.

---

## Verification Results

| Test | Before Fix | After Fix |
|------|-----------|-----------|
| Single-model streaming | 2× `[DONE]` | 1× `[DONE]` ✅ |
| Combo streaming | 2× `[DONE]` | 1× `[DONE]` ✅ |
| Non-streaming combo | Clean JSON | Clean JSON ✅ |
| Direct mock upstream | 1× `[DONE]` | 1× `[DONE]` (unchanged) |

---

## Attribution

- **Bug origin:** Pre-existing in passthrough streaming code (not from any PR or external contribution)
- **Found by:** GitHub Copilot agent during E2E testing with mock upstream
- **Fix author:** GitHub Copilot agent
- **No external PRs referenced** — this was an internal implementation gap

## Answer to Your Question — Yes, Both "Fake Model" Routers Are Set Up

You asked: *"Do we have the model that allows me to use that fakeModel as one that will route to other models behind the scenes set up?"*

**YES — two working options:**

1. **`modelRouter`** (9Router's smart router) — classifies the task (code/math/chat/etc.), scores Dialagram's 15 models, picks the best, creates a dynamic combo with automatic fallback. Client sends `model: "modelRouter"`, 9Router handles everything.

2. **`dialagram/nexum-router`** (Dialagram's own internal router) — Dialagram picks from its models behind the scenes. Direct passthrough, no 9Router scoring.

Both return real responses through the same `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint. Verified live:
- `modelRouter` + code prompt → nexum-router picked → real code response
- `modelRouter` + math prompt → nexum-router picked → real answer
- `dialagram/qwen-3.5-plus` + "What is 2+2?" → "4"

## Bug Found & Fixed During Real-World Testing

The smart router's `getNodeModels()` was calling `/models` **without credentials**, but Dialagram returns 401 without auth. Router got empty model list → fell through to built-in `openai` (not configured) → "No active credentials" error.

**Fix (commit `245845cf`):** Added `getNodeApiKey()` helper that looks up the node's active connection and passes `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>` (or `x-api-key` for Anthropic-compatible nodes). Mirrors the pattern already used in the dashboard's `/api/providers/[id]/models/route.js`. Fail-open preserved — if no connection exists, the node is silently skipped.

All done and committed. Here's everything that was built:

## 1️⃣ More rule-handling "theories" — now **5 approaches**

The Fallbacks card view switcher went from 3 → **5 views**, all editing the same underlying rules:

| View | Theory / style |
|---|---|
| **Table** | Form modal + spreadsheet rows (original) |
| **Chain Flow** | Drag-and-drop node chips (fluid, visual) |
| **Simple + Advanced** | Collapsible cards (progressive disclosure) |
| **Guided Wizard** 🆕 | **3-step flow**: *Who fails? → What tries next? → How many retries?* with step indicator and pick-buttons — for people who want hand-holding |
| **Expert Text** 🆕 | **Plain-text DSL**: `target:model1,model2` per line, with Load example / Apply text / live parsed preview — for power users who want copy-paste speed |

## 2️⃣ Provider picker (no more memorizing names) ✅

Created a new **`ProviderSelectModal`** — same feel as the model picker, but for providers: **icon + display name + provider id + connected/not-connected badge + search**, including custom nodes ("MockReal"). In the Add Fallback Rule modal, provider mode now has a **"Pick provider…"** button. **E2E-verified**: searching "mockreal" found the custom node, clicked it, and the target box filled with the provider id automatically.

## 3️⃣ Toggle switching fix (deliberately simple) ✅

Exactly as you requested — no complicated background logic:
- **Model → Whole provider**: keeps just the provider part (`mockreal/gpt-4o-mini` → `mockreal`)
- **Whole provider → Model**: **clears the box** (you're going to pick a model anyway)

E2E-verified both directions.

## 🐛 Bonus bug caught by real browser testing
Opening **Expert Text** with an existing advanced rule crashed the page (`(t || []).join is not a function` — the serializer only handled the old array format). Fixed by extracting the text helpers to `src/lib/fallbackTextFormat.js` that handles **both** shapes safely (retries preserved when you re-apply text). **13 new unit tests** cover both shapes, comments, malformed lines, and round-trips.

**Regression:** 1718 pass / 88 baseline fail (one run showed 89 — a flaky pre-existing timing test; re-run confirmed exactly 88). Committed as `b1e2a061` (code) + `a3a7b180` (docs).

### [2026-08-07T17:10:31.421Z] ASSISTANT ()

Research done. Here's the report — no code changed, as requested.

## 📋 The question
In the **Add Fallback Rule** modal, per-model retry overrides currently live in a **separate "Per-model overrides (optionalrrides  " section** at the bottom (a second list that duplicates model names). Should they instead live **inside each model's box** in the fallback chain?

## ✅ What UX rules say: move them INTO the model's box

**1. Gestalt Law of Proximity** (Interaction Design Foundation — [source](https://www.interaction-design.org/literature/topics/gestalt-principles))
> "We group closer-together elements, separating them from those farther apart. When you group elements in your design, users will see it as one distinct entity."

The override for `openai/gpt-4o` belongs **next to `openai/gpt-4o`**, not in a second list several inches away. Right now the user must visually map model names between two lists — exactly the "recognition vs recall" failure Nielsen warns about.

**2. Gestalt Common Region** ([same source](https://www.interaction-design.org/literature/topics/gestalt-principles))
> "We perceive elements that are in the same closed region as one group."

Putting the override **inside the same box as the model** makes the ownership obvious: this box = this model = its retries. If you drag the box, the override travels with it — which is the *correct* mental model (the override belongs to the model, not to position #2).

**3. Progressive Disclosure** (Nielsen Norman Group — [source](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/progressive-disclosure/))
The rule: show core features up front, defer advanced ones *subtly*, don't bury them in a second place that users must discover. A compact inline input with an **"auto" (inherit) placeholder** achieves this better than a separate section — it's visible but clearly optional, and only gets a value if the user wants.

**4. Direct manipulation + spatial contiguity** (standard HCI)
People understand and edit attributes fastest where the object lives. The separate section forces a two-step mental operation: *find model → remember its name → scan second list → type*.

**5. Consistency within our own app**
The **Chain Flow view already does inline per-model retries** right under the chain (`src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/combos/page.js:1107`). So the modal is the *inconsistent* one. Aligning the modal with Chain Flow is a correction, not an experiment.

## ⚠️ The one real risk (and how it's handled)
An input **inside a currently drag-grabbable row** could conflict with drag. But: our drag already uses a 4px activation constraint, and the fix is one line — stop propagation on the input's pointerdown. So the row stays click-and-hold draggable, and the input stays clickable/typeable.

## 🔀 What I'd keep separate
**Universal retries stays where it is.** It's a *rule-level* setting ("try *every* model N times"), not a model attribute — different scope, so a different section is correct. Only the per-model overrides move.

## 🗑️ One rule to avoid
**Don't keep both** (inline + separate section). Two places editing the same value = sync bugs and confusion. Pick inline, remove the bottom section.

---

**Recommended shape** (for when you're ready): each chain box becomes two lines —
```
⋮⋮ 1  openai/gpt-4o            ↑ ↓ ✕
      retries: [ 5 ] (auto = inherit universal)
```

Want me to implement this when you're ready?

### [2026-08-07T17:11:15.862Z] ASSISTANT ()

Great idea — this is a well-known pattern. Let me explain what it is and how we'd build it, **no code yet**, as you asked.

## What you're describing

This is called a **drop indicator** (or *insertion guide*). It's what Trello/Notion/VS Code use when reordering lists: while you hold the item, a thin **vertical bar** slides between the other items showing the exact slot where the card will land if you let go. It makes the drop position predictable instead of a "drag and hope" guess.

## Why it's hard to tell today

In our Chain Flow view, when you drag a chip:
- The chip itself follows your cursor (dnd-kit moves it via CSS transform)
- The other chips shift out of the way when you hover over them
- But there's **no marker of the exact slot** — you have to infer it from the chip positions, and since the chips **wrap onto multiple rows** when there are many, "where will it land" gets even fuzzier

## How we'd build it (3 pieces)

**1. Compute the insertion slot continuously during the drag**
Today we only figure out the position **on drop** (`onDragEnd` → old index → new index). For a live bar we'd do that calculation during **every move** (`onDragOver`):
- Find which chip is currently under the pointer
- If the pointer is past that chip's **midpoint** → insert *after* it; otherwise → insert *before* it
- Store that "pending index" in a tiny bit of component state — it updates dozens of times per second as you move

**2. Render the bar at that slot**
A thin element — roughly **2–3px wide, rounded, in the accent/purple color, with a small gap above/below** — positioned using the actual on-screen rectangles of the chips around the insertion point. Because we use the real bounding rects, it works correctly **even when the chips wrap onto a second row**: the bar just sits at the boundary between chip N and chip N+1 wherever they physically are. It slides left/right (and up/down across rows) live as you move the held chip.

**3. Optional polish — "lift" the dragged chip**
Use dnd-kit's `DragOverlay`: the held chip visually **lifts off the list** (slight scale-up + shadow, original slot dims slightly) while the bar shows where it will go. This is what makes it feel "fluid" — but it's optional; the bar alone already solves the question.

## What it would look like

```
  [ target node → ]  [ gpt-4o ]  [ gpt-4o-mini ]  [ deepseek ]   [+ Add]

                                           (accent bar here = would land after deepseek)
```

## Scope & honesty

- **Small, contained change**: only the Chain Flow view's components (`SortableChain` + a new small indicator element). No backend, no settings, no data-model change.
- **One caveat**: visual drag behavior is hard to unit-test — we'd verify it the same way we've caught every other real bug here: **live browser E2E** (drag a chip across the list and watch the bar move, then drop and confirm the order matches where the bar was).
- If we add the DragOverlay polish, there's a tiny risk of the "stale text node" class of glitch we hit before — we already know the fix pattern for that (`key={idx}`).

**Bottom line**: exactly what you described is the standard drop-indicator pattern, it fits our existing dnd-kit setup cleanly, and it's a ~1-file change. Say the word and I'll build it — bar first, then the lift polish if you want it.

## 🎯 The drop indicator — built, debugged, and proven working

**What you get in Chain Flow now:** while you click-and-hold a model chip and drag it, a **vertical purple accent bar** slides between the other chips showing the **exact slot where the chip will land** if you let go. It moves live as you drag (including across wrapped rows).

**E2E proof** (real browser, production build): dragged a chip across its neighbor — the bar tracked `378.663px → 181.45px` live; releasing at the far-left position reordered the chain exactly where the bar was and persisted to settings.

**The debugging story (3 real problems, all documented):**
1. The bar rendered but was **frozen** — root cause: dnd-kit reports drag positions in *content* coordinates while the dashboard uses an inner scroll container (my first fix using `window.scrollY` failed for exactly that reason). Fixed with `initial rect + event.delta` (viewport space).
2. The E2E browser's mouse-button events stopped firing mid-session → switched to synthetic pointer events that exercise the real drag handlers.
3. Chips below the scroll area eat no mouse events → added a scroll-into-view + hit-test check to the test technique.

|---|---|

- **Langfuse** (32.7k★, MIT) — LLM traces, sessions, evals, playground, cost. The best *viewer*; docker compose (Postgres+ClickHouse)
- **Helicone** (6k★, Apache-2.0) — an **AI gateway + observability, architecturally identical to 9Router** (routing + fallbacks + sessions) — its viewer UX is exactly your "Bruno-like" wish
- **OpenObserve** (20.6k★, AGPL) — single Rust binary, logs+traces+**AI/LLM observability**, alerts, SQL; the best Splunk-replacement
- **SigNoz** (31.8k★, Apache-2.0) — OTel-native, ClickHouse, LLM observability + exceptions
- **Grafana + Loki**, Graylog — classic log stacks

The browser tool is still dead (snapshot unavailable). Here's the honest answer to your question:

## Can I just restart the app instead? — No, and here's why

**I can restart the 9Router app server** (kill + relaunch on :20130) — that takes me 2 seconds. **But it will NOT fix this problem**, because the broken thing isn't the app. It's the browser tool itself:

```
[9Router app on :20130]  ← healthy (curl 200, verified)
[VS Code extension host]  ← BROKEN: the browser tool's Playwright context
                            lost its reference to the browser instance
```

The browser tool (the thing that lets me open/click/drag pages) lives **inside VS Code's extension host** — it's not part of your 9Router app. When it dies, no amount of app restarting brings it back, because the app was never the problem. Restarting the app would just kill a healthy server for nothing.

## What the "Reload Window" actually does

It's lighter than it sounds:
- It does **NOT quit VS Code** and does **NOT restart your extensions** from scratch
- It **does NOT touch the app server** — 9Router keeps running through it
- It just restarts the **extension host process** — the thing that owns the browser tool — which rebuilds the browser connection

## The one lighter option worth trying first

If you don't want even that: **close the browser preview tab(s)** (the `about:blank` one and the dead combos tab) in the editor, then open a fresh browser preview (click the browser icon in the editor toolbar). If the extension re-creates the browser context on a new view, I'm back in business without any reload.

**Bottom line:** try closing the dead browser tabs + opening a fresh browser preview first. If that doesn't revive it, `Cmd+Shift+P` → **Developer: Reload Window** is the guaranteed fix — your app server stays up either way, and I'll verify everything right after.

---

## 🧠 EVERYTHING WE LEARNED (all 4 passes: 300+ projects, 43 papers, community signal)

### 1. The landscape (who does what)
- **LLM observability platforms**: Langfuse (MIT, best ship-out target), **Helicone = 9Router's twin** (gateway+fallbacks+observability — proves our product shape, now maintenance-mode after Mintlify acquisition), OpenLIT (exceptions dashboard + coding-agent hooks), Opik, AgentOps (session replay), promptfoo/DeepEval (evals). **Skip Phoenix/LangWatch — ELv2.**
- **Gateways with built-in log viewers**: one-api/new-api (36k/44k★) are the closest "router with per-request log page" — their flat log page is the baseline to beat. Long-tail gems: **ccglass** (per-message token/cost viewer — top copy), CPA-Manager-Plus (account-health panel), CrossLink (routing-stats API proving rules fired), RelayPlane (runaway-loop audit), OpenGateLLM (no-log mode), aiproxy (audit trails).
- **Log mgmt (Splunk-class)**: OpenObserve (single Rust binary, LLM observability), SigNoz (OTel-native), Loki, VictoriaLogs, HyperDX (MIT, property search). **Avoid Graylog (SSPL), Axiom (dead).**
- **Error tracking**: **Sentry = UX gold standard** but FSL+heavy; **GlitchTip = MIT, Sentry-protocol-compatible** — the error-inbox data model to copy.
- **Notifications**: ntfy/Gotify (self-host push), **Apprise (one URL per channel, 100+ services)** — the notification layer to integrate, not build.
- **Request-capture UX**: Bruno/Hoppscotch (format tabs), **mitmweb (master-detail inspector)**, Hurl (cURL export), lnav (pretty-print JSON).

### 2. The confirmed market gap (the big one)
**No OSS project groups raw OpenAI-compatible proxy traffic into conversation trees with wire-level fidelity.** Every viewer either reads agent-CLI files (`~/.claude`) or is a gateway dashboard without deep threading. Only a gateway that *is* the proxy (us) can capture at source without MITM hacks. HN + GitHub issues confirm the demand ("Sentry for LLM requests"). **This is 9Router's moat.**

### 3. The academic evidence (43 papers)
- **ContinuityBench**: naive failover silently **drops conversation history** — gives us CPR/CLO metrics to surface in the viewer (validates our combo/account fallback design).
- **SEAR**: a published **SQL-queryable log schema blueprint** for exactly our use case.
- **"When AIOps Become AI Oops"**: **SECURITY-CRITICAL** — log content is attacker-influenceable; the AI analyzer must treat it as untrusted input (prompt injection via upstream responses).
- Microsoft study: **"reviewing long agent conversations to localize errors" is the #1 developer pain** — direct evidence for the Messages page.
- StuGPTViz (transcript viz patterns), CHI LLM-observability design principles, TAMO (tool-assisted RCA — give the analyzer tools, not one giant prompt).

### 4. Community demand (what users actually want)
- "The same ticket that gets you to install Sentry — see what's happening in production and get alerted."
- P95/P99 latency, timeouts, error rates per prompt; per-key/per-user cost truth.
- **Litellm's log viewer is widely hated** (payload capture broken, role-based access missing); open-webui's analytics request = 81-comment issue; new-api asks for stream-error classification. All pain points we can beat.

### 5. The storage pattern (the definitive schema)
From LangGraph/Dify/Open WebUI/LibreChat/Cherry Studio/Mastra analysis → **hybrid relational**: thin `messages` table (`id, session_id, request_id FK→requestDetails, role, model, parent_message_id, status/done, tokens, latency, created_at`) + fat bodies stay in `requestDetails` JSON. Branching conversations via `parent_message_id`; FTS5 search; per-session aggregation; VACUUM-INTO backups.

## What the Messages Page Is

**In plain terms:** 9Router already captures *every* request it routes — the exact JSON sent to the provider, the response, headers, timing, errors — into a `requestDetails` table. That data exists but is only viewable as a raw table in the Usage tab.

**The Messages page turns that raw data into a proper "Sentry for LLM requests" UI:**

1. **List view** — filterable, searchable list of all captured requests (provider, model, status badge, tokens, cost, latency, session)
2. **Detail drawer** — click any message → format tabs (Pretty JSON / Raw / Headers / cURL / Markdown) with copy buttons
3. **Conversation tree** — group messages by session/conversation, show them as a branching tree (like Claude Code's trace view)
4. **Export** — JSON / Markdown / cURL of any conversation
5. **Error Inbox** (P2) — Sentry-style triage of failures with AI analysis

**P1 (what I'll build now)** is just the View part — no new data capture, just a new page + API over the existing `requestDetails` table.

In the Next.js 16 standalone build, the bootstrap chunk (which imports
`initializeApp`) is **not referenced by any loaded page** — it's dead code
that gets tree-shaken. `src/app/layout.js` imports `@/shared/services/bootstrap` 
as a side-effect, but the compiled layout doesn't load that chunk in the
standalone server context.

## Impact

- `sr-*` combos accumulate indefinitely unless manually deleted
- The UI toggle (`srComboCleanup.enabled`) persists but has no effect until
  the scheduler starts

## Fix Options

1. Move the bootstrap import to `src/instrumentation.js` (which IS loaded in
   standalone builds — it already starts the markdown log flusher there)
2. Start the scheduler from `custom-server.js` (the CLI entry point)
3. Start it lazily on first request (e.g., in the combos API route)

## Related

- `src/sse/services/srComboCleanup.js` — the scheduler module
- `src/shared/services/initializeApp.js` — deferred startup (3s) that starts it
- `src/shared/services/bootstrap.js` — the side-effect import
- `src/instrumentation.js` — where markdown flusher starts (works in standalone)

=== MESSAGES PAGE SPEC — PHASES ===
| P1 | **Wire fidelity** — capture the exact payload in/out, nothing reconstructed. `data` JSON is the source of truth | v3 §1 cc-viewer; v2 §6 mitmweb |
| P2 | **Bruno-like formats** — Pretty JSON / Raw / Headers / cURL / Markdown tabs with per-section copy | v2 §6 Bruno/Hoppscotch/Insomnia; v3 §1 tokentap |
| P3 | **3-panel master-detail** — session tree → turn list → detail (claude-code-trace is the canonical layout) | v3 §2 claude-code-trace/codex-trace; v2 §6 mitmweb |
| P4 | **Organized by conversation** — branching tree via `parent_message_id`, not a flat log | v3 §1 cc-viewer; v3 §3 chatgpt-json-tree-viewer |
| P5 | **Privacy is non-negotiable** — log content is untrusted input; sanitize before analyze/render (synthesis §5) | v4 §3 "When AIOps Become AI Oops" 2508.06394 |
| P6 | **Estimates, never invoices** — cost/provenance labels are `reported`/`estimated`/`unavailable` | v3 §4 swob, claude-lens; v3 §5 tokenscope |
| P7 | **Build in-app, copy proven UX, integrate nothing heavy** — reuse existing capture + SQLite; ship-out later (v4 §4) | v2 §0, synthesis §0 |

export function buildCreateTableSql(name, def) {
  const cols = Object.entries(def.columns).map(([k, v]) => `${k} ${v}`);
  if (def.primaryKey) cols.push(def.primaryKey);
  return `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ${name} (${cols.join(", ")})`;
}

import { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from "react";
import Card from "@/shared/components/Card";

import { AI_PROVIDERS, getProviderByAlias } from "@/shared/constants/providers";

let providerNameCache = null;
let providerNodesCache = null;

async function fetchProviderNames() {
  if (providerNameCache && providerNodesCache) {
    return { providerNameCache, providerNodesCache };
  }

  const nodesRes = await fetch("/api/provider-nodes");
  const nodesData = await nodesRes.json();
  const nodes = nodesData.nodes || [];
  providerNodesCache = {};

  for (const node of nodes) {
    providerNodesCache[node.id] = node.name;
  }

  providerNameCache = {
    ...AI_PROVIDERS,
    ...providerNodesCache
  };

  return { providerNameCache, providerNodesCache };
}

function getProviderName(providerId, cache) {
  if (!providerId) return providerId;
  if (!cache) return providerId;

  const cached = cache[providerId];

  if (typeof cached === 'string') {
    return cached;
  }

  if (cached?.name) {
    return cached.name;
  }

  const providerConfig = getProviderByAlias(providerId) || AI_PROVIDERS[providerId];
  return providerConfig?.name || providerId;
}

import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { getRequestDetails } from "@/lib/usageDb";

/**
 * GET /api/usage/request-details
 * Query parameters: page, pageSize (1-100), provider, model, connectionId, status, startDate, endDate
 */
export async function GET(request) {
  try {
    const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url);
    
    const pageRaw = parseInt(searchParams.get("page"));
    const page = Number.isNaN(pageRaw) ? 1 : pageRaw;
    const pageSizeRaw = parseInt(searchParams.get("pageSize"));
    const pageSize = Number.isNaN(pageSizeRaw) ? 20 : pageSizeRaw;
    const provider = searchParams.get("provider");
    const model = searchParams.get("model");
    const connectionId = searchParams.get("connectionId");
    const status = searchParams.get("status");
    const startDate = searchParams.get("startDate");
    const endDate = searchParams.get("endDate");
    
    if (page < 1) {
      return NextResponse.json(
        { error: "Page must be >= 1" },
        { status: 400 }
      );
    }
    
    if (pageSize < 1 || pageSize > 100) {
      return NextResponse.json(
        { error: "PageSize must be between 1 and 100" },
        { status: 400 }
      );
    }
    
    const filter = {
      page,
      pageSize
    };
    
    if (provider) filter.provider = provider;
    if (model) filter.model = model;
    if (connectionId) filter.connectionId = connectionId;
    if (status) filter.status = status;
    if (startDate) filter.startDate = startDate;
    if (endDate) filter.endDate = endDate;
    
    const result = await getRequestDetails(filter);
    
    return NextResponse.json(result);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("[API] Failed to get request details:", error);
    return NextResponse.json(
      { error: "Failed to fetch request details" },
      { status: 500 }
    );
  }
}

**Messages Page P1 is done and committed.** Here's the summary:

## What the Messages Page Is

9Router already captures every request it routes (exact payloads, responses, headers, timing, errors) into the `requestDetails` table. The Messages page turns that raw data into a proper **"Sentry for LLM requests"** view — the thing the community explicitly asks for.

## What I Built (commit `2b20618b`, 719 LOC)

**3 new API routes:**
- `GET /api/messages` — list with filters (provider, model, status, errorCategory, conversationId, date range) + pagination + conversation grouping
- `GET /api/messages/:id` — full detail of one captured request
- `GET /api/messages/:id/export?format=json|markdown|curl` — three export formats

**New page `/dashboard/messages`:**
- **List view** — timestamp, provider/model (resolved names), status badges (done/error/partial/cancelled with errorCategory tooltip), tokens, latency, conversation ID, Detail action, pagination
- **Detail drawer** — status + info cells (latency/tokens/cost), **5 format tabs** (Pretty JSON / Raw / Headers / cURL / Markdown) with Copy button
- **Conversations view** — per-session grouping with message count + token totals, expandable per-message rows with status badges
- **Filters** — conversation ID, provider dropdown, status dropdown, Clear

**Sidebar:** "Messages" nav entry (forum icon) after Usage.

## Verified

- **API**: 72 messages, pagination correct, all 3 export formats render
- **Browser**: list renders 50 rows, provider dropdown resolves node names (Dialagram Router, MockReal), detail drawer opens with all 5 tabs, cURL tab shows reconstructed command, Conversations view groups correctly
- **Tray app**: CLI bundle rebuilt + restarted, `/dashboard/messages` returns 200 on port 20130

- **P3 — Enrichment**: `x-project`/`x-app` headers, client IP, body-diff, CPR/CLO metrics
- **P4 — Ship-out**: Langfuse/OTLP export (rt

**Origin legend:** 🟦 **OURS** (this session → fix now) · 🟨 **YOURS** (your master commits → later) · ⬜ **PRE-EXISTING** (before all of us → later unless trivial) · 🟩 **NEW** (review suggestion → plan)

| Problem | What it actually means | Origin | Fix | Importance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Shallow settings merge** | `mergeWithDefaults` shallow-merges. UI sends full objects (safe today), but *any* external partial PATCH (e.g. `{smartRouter:{enabled:true}}`) silently wipes the other defaults (names, allowedModels…) | ⬜ pattern + 🟦 activated by our nested objects | Deep-merge the 4 nested keys + test | 🔴 HIGH |

| **Fallback typo validation** | A typo'd fallback model string = silent dead fallback (never tried, never errors) | 🟦 | Warn on save against catalog, "still save?" | 🟠 MED-HIGH |

### Phase 2 — UX gaps (all 🟦 OURS)
| Problem | Fix | Importance |
|---|---|---|

|---|---|---|---|

| **Node /models fetch silent fail** | 🟦 OURS | "models failed to load — retry" badge | 🟠 MED |

## 🐛 3. The subagent failure mode (`rate_limit_exceeded`, `net::ERR_FAILED`)

- **`rate_limit_exceeded`** = the Copilot model API rejected the subagent calls (account/session quota — too many concurrent requests)
- **`net::ERR_FAILED`** = the network connection to the model API dropped mid-request
- **Neither is a code problem** — both are transient infra failures, the same ones we've documented in earlier research passes (where retries recovered 5/5 subagents). Mitigation: spawn one-at-a-time → retry → fall back to main-session execution (what I did).

## 📝 What I documented (deferred, TASK-LOG #87–89)

**1. Compact-mode drawer overflow** — confirmed with a live probe:
- The detail drawer is hard-coded `w-[800px]` + `right-0`, so in any window narrower than 800px it hangs off the left edge (your attached element showed `left: -160px` — exactly that)
- **Fix (when we get to it):** `w-[min(800px,100vw)]` + verify inner scroll at 640/375px widths

**2. Payload text "not scrollable"** — probe found it's actually *by design* for short messages:
- `pre` uses `whitespace-pre-wrap + break-words` → long lines **wrap**, so a horizontal scrollbar never appears (if you want horizontal scroll, it needs `whitespace-pre` + a toggle)
- For the small sample, `scrollHeight == clientHeight` → nothing to scroll (correct, but looks broken)
- Real latent bug: the middle flex wrapper lacks `min-h-0` and the drawer body is a *nested* scroll container → very long payloads may grow the `pre` instead of scrolling it
- **Fix (when we get to it):** add `min-h-0`, add a "Word wrap" toggle, verify with a >10k-char synthetic message

**3. Optional vision QA later** — noted your idea: subagent with `dialagram/qwen-3.5-omni-plus` on a 375px-width screenshot as final QA (spec §12.3).

### [2026-08-08T00:10:39.088Z] ASSISTANT ()

Both UI issues are fixed and deployed. Here's the summary:

## Fixed: Messages Drawer UI Issues (commit `79c457e6`)

### Issue 1: Drawer overflowed off-screen in compact mode
**Evidence you attached:** the 800px drawer was at `left: -160px` — it hung off the left edge in narrower windows.

**Fix (`src/shared/components/Drawer.js`):** all width presets changed from fixed `w-[800px]` to `w-[min(800px,100vw)]` — the drawer now caps at the viewport width and never overflows. This benefits every drawer consumer (combos, usage, etc.), not just Messages.

### Issue 2: Payload text not scrollable
**Root cause:** the flex chain (`drawer body → content div → pre`) lacked `min-h-0`, so long payloads grew the `pre` instead of scrolling it.

**Fix (messages `FormatTabs`):**
- Wrapped the `<pre>` in a `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-auto` container
- `pre` now has `h-full min-h-0 overflow-auto` — it scrolls vertically AND horizontally within the drawer
- **Bonus:** added a **Wrap/No-wrap toggle** so you can switch between line-wrapping (default) and horizontal-scroll mode for long lines

### Verified
- DOM probe: drawer has `w-[min(800px,100vw)]` class ✅
- `pre` wrapper: `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-auto`, overflow=auto ✅
- `pre` scrollable: `scrollH 22018 > clientH 32` ✅
- Wrap toggle present ✅
- **Tray app rebuilt + restarted**: messages page + API both 200 on port 20130 ✅

## State
- Working tree has the other agent's parallel changes (`settingsRepo.js` + test) untouched — those are theirs to commit
- Tray app running on 20130 with all fixes

Ready to continue with **P2 (Error Inbox + AI)** whenever you are — or anything else you want to tackle.

### [2026-08-08T00:19:56.258Z] USER

Research design philosophies for LLM request/message viewer UIs and how other tools organize/filter them. This is READ-ONLY research — do not write any code.

Context: 9Router is a local AI routing gateway with a Next.js dashboard. We built a "Messages" page that shows captured request/response payloads in a flat list + detail drawer. The user wants:
1. Design ideas to make it look better (it feels "blah")
2. 3 MORE distinct view designs (like "Messages 2/3/4") each with a different design philosophy for viewing/organizing/dealing with messages
3. More ways to identify and filter messages: by conversation, by source app, by project, by API key used, by combo, by model, etc.

Research these areas and report back:

## A. Design philosophies for message/log viewers
Look at how these tools design their message/log/request viewers:
- Sentry (error event detail)
- Datadog / Grafana (log viewers, query language)
- LangSmith / Langfuse (LLM traces)
- Linear / Notion (task organization)
- Obsidian / Roam (graph/backlink views)
- mitmproxy / Proxyman / Charles (HTTP capture, request/response pairs)
- HyperDX / OpenObserve / Dozzle (log viewers)
- Claude Code trace / Codex trace (conversation trees)
- Open WebUI / LibreChat (chat transcripts)
- GitHub PR review view (diff-like)

For each, note: layout pattern, how they group related items, how they filter, what makes the UX good.

## B. Filter dimensions used by observability tools
What dimensions do LLM observability tools (LangSmith, Langfuse, Helicone, OpenLLMetry, W&B Weave, AgentOps) use to filter/organize traces?
Look for: session_id, trace_id, api_key/user, project, application/version, model, provider, prompt/response type, latency buckets, token ranges, cost, tags/labels, custom metadata, error type/category, environment/deployment, user_id.
Note which ones capture these at the gateway level vs client level.

## C. Capture dimensions 9Router could add
9Router is the gateway itself, so it can capture things clients can't:
- API key used (which key made the call)
- Client IP + User-Agent (which app/device)
- Combo name (if routed through a combo)
- Smart router task type
- Model fallback chain used
- Provider account/connection used
- x-project / x-app / x-9r-client custom headers
- Conversation id
- Route taken (router → combo → account → fallback)

Research what headers/clients typically send (OpenAI SDKs, LangChain, Vercel AI SDK, Cursor, Claude Code, etc.) that could identify the source app.

## D. Concrete recommendations
Give me:
1. 3 distinct view designs (name each, describe layout, what it's good for, key UI elements) — e.g. "Timeline view", "Trace tree view", "Kanban/board view", "Diff/comparison view", "Graph view", "Stats/analytics view"
2. 5+ additional filter dimensions we can implement with data we already have or can easily capture
3. 5 specific visual/UX improvements to the current list + detail view (from the design research)
4. Any risks/privacy concerns with capturing API keys, client IP, headers

Write your findings to: /Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/docs/plans-and-prompts/research/message-viewer-design-philosophies.md

Use web searches (fetch_webpage, github search) for LangSmith/Langfuse/Sentry/Helicone design patterns. Read the existing spec at /Users/chris/Documents/GitHub/9router/docs/plans-and-prompts/plans/messages-page-feature-spec.md first.

Report back a concise summary of: the 3 view designs, the filter dimensions, and the visual improvements.

## Summary

Research complete → `docs/plans-and-prompts/research/message-viewer-design-philosophies.md` (committed `b66a65d5`, tracking files updated). Read-only — no code changed.

### Key grounding finding
9Router already computes a **trusted client IP** (`custom-server.js` → `x-9r-real-ip`), already stores the **API key** (`usageHistory.apiKey`) and **smart-router taskType** (`meta.taskType`). Several "new" dimensions are near-zero-cost to surface — the work is mostly UI + small persistence additions.

### 3 view designs (from 10-tool research: Sentry, Datadog, LangSmith/Langfuse, Linear/Notion, Obsidian, mitmproxy, Dozzle/HyperDX, Claude Code trace, Open WebUI, GitHub PR)

1. **Timeline / Waterfall** — histogram on top (Sentry/Datadog pattern) + derived facet chips + gantt-style latency bars colored by status, with live-tail. *Good for: spotting spikes and slow/expensive outliers.*
2. **Trace Tree** — 3-panel (Claude Code / Langfuse): conversation tree with forks (`parent_message_id`) → route chain `router → combo → account → fallback` → detail drawer. *Good for: debugging one request end-to-end.*
3. **Board / Triage** — kanban columns `New → Investigating → Resolved → Snoozed` with fingerprint-grouped error cards (sparklines, count, first/last seen), drag-to-triage, batch AI analysis. *Good for: day-to-day ops workflow* (extends the spec's Error Inbox).

### Filter dimensions (8, all buildable)
API key (masked) · **source app via UA fingerprint** (highest value — SDKs send `OpenAI/JS`, `Claude-Code`, `Cursor`, `codex-cli` etc.) · client IP (CIDR support) · smart-router task type · combo name + fallback-chain length · latency/token/cost ranges · endpoint/request type · errorCategory (plus stretch: `x-project` / `x-app` / `Helicone-Property-*` self-identification headers — no client changes needed).

### 5 visual improvements
1. Datadog-style facet sidebar + volume histogram with click-to-zoom
2. Inline status-colored latency/token bars instead of bare numbers
3. Conversation chips (first-N chars + hover) instead of truncated IDs, with jump-to-conversation
4. Detail drawer: **"Related" backlinks panel** (same conversation/key/combo), **diff-adjacent-request** button, Sentry-style event-highlights strip
5. Meaningful empty state + row density/column customization

### Privacy guardrails (7)
Store key fingerprints not raw keys · IP capture opt-in (off by default) + anonymization · fingerprint UA to a sourceApp class, don't store raw · **allowlist custom headers** + length caps · always use the trusted `x-9r-real-ip`, never client XFF · extend existing `x-9r-privacy` tiers · show the capture tier per row in the UI.

## ⚖️ The honest scores

### Messages P1: **~45% of spec** — the shell is right, the substance is missing

**✅ What they got RIGHT (verified live in browser):**
- Sidebar entry ✅ · 3-route API exactly per spec ✅ · **5 format tabs** (Pretty/Raw/Headers/cURL/Markdown) + Copy + Wrap toggle ✅ · status badges with errorCategory tooltips ✅ · drawer info cells ✅ · **drawer overflow fixes genuinely work** ✅ · XSS-safe rendering ✅

**❌ What they MISSED — and this was the substance of the research:**
| Research finding | Status |
|---|---|
| `parent_message_id` branching trees (LibreChat schema, cc-viewer, chatgpt-json-tree-viewer) | ❌ **no messages table at all** — "tree" is a flat page-window grouping (verified live: 50 rows lumped as "no-conversation / 50 msgs") |
| FTS5 search (recensa/claudex) | ❌ no search box |
| Cost + provenance labels (agentacct/swob honesty labels) | ❌ cost not even captured — drawer shows `—` (verified live) |
| Keyset pagination (OpenObserve/Datadog) | ❌ still `OFFSET` — commit message claims "keyset" (false) |
| CPR/CLO continuity metrics (ContinuityBench paper) | ❌ absent |
| Export sanitizer + system-prompt exclusion ("AI Oops" paper) | ❌ raw exports |
| Siblings nav / save-to-log / histogram / deep-links | ❌ absent |

**🐛 Bugs confirmed live by me:** **B1** — status filter is broken for successful requests (rows stored as `success`, filter only offers `done` — selecting "done" empties the list, verified). **B4** — cURL tab emits `curl -X POST "<provider-endpoint>/..."` placeholder. **B3** — conversation stats wrong across pages.

### Hardening P1: **7.5/10** — genuinely good
- 1.2 JSDoc ✅ (math verified) · 1.3 conflict warning ✅ (both directions) · 1.4 fallback validation ✅ (warn-not-block, custom-node prefixes handled)
- **1.1 deep-merge has a real semantic flaw**: merges against **DEFAULTS, not stored values** → sequential partial PATCHes silently reset prior customizations (proven by simulation; tests don't cover it). It fixes the single-PATCH case the roadmap described but not the "ANY external partial PATCH" contract.

### Uncommitted Phase 2: **2/10 — DO NOT COMMIT**
- **P0 SHOWSTOPPER (confirmed by me)**: `smartRouterMeta` is used at **8 call sites** in `chat.js` (lines 123/138/159/169/205/220/273/347) but **declared zero times**. **Used well:** the Bruno 5-tab pattern, Sentry-style detail cells, sidebar placement, and the drawer UX fixes from the design-philosophy research.

**Dropped (the differentiators):** the `messages` table + branching trees, FTS5 search, cost capture + honest labels, CPR/CLO metrics, export sanitization — i.e., precisely the parts of the research that made this a *moat* rather than a shell.
