# 9Router Messages Page — Code Audit

## 1. React bugs

### B1. `BoardView` — setState during render (React anti-pattern, can loop)
**File:** `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/messages/components/BoardView.js`
**Lines:** 55–63 (`if (!seeded && grouped.length > 0) { setSeeded(true); … setColumns(next); }`)
**Severity:** **Major**
**Description:** The "seed" logic calls `setSeeded(true)` and `setColumns(next)` directly during render. React officially forbids this ("Cannot update a component while rendering a different component" is only tolerated for the *same* component's state in a narrow pattern; here it's a state update during render that also reads `columns` from the closure). Worse, the guard is broken: `setSeeded(true)` is queued, but the render continues with the *old* `columns` — and because `seeded` is still `false` in this render, if React re-renders before the state flush (e.g., a parent re-render from `openDetail`), the seed block runs again and **duplicates groups into `new`** (the `Object.values(next).flat().some(...)` dedupe check runs against the stale `columns`, not `next`). Also, `grouped` is recomputed on every `messages` change (new page/filter), but seeding only happens once — new fingerprints from a filter change are never added to the board, and stale fingerprints from the previous filter remain (see B2).
**Suggested fix:** Move seeding into a `useEffect` keyed on `grouped` (or better, derive column membership with a `useMemo` that merges `grouped` into `new` deterministically, keeping only user moves in state).

### B2. `BoardView` — stale board state across filter/page changes
**File:** `BoardView.js`
**Lines:** 55–63 (seed-once), 65–72 (`move`), 74 (`allGrouped` unused)
**Severity:** **Major**
**Description:** `columns` is initialized once and only mutated by drags. When the parent fetches a new page or applies a filter, `messages` changes → `grouped` changes → new fingerprints never appear on the board, and fingerprints no longer in the data stay pinned in their columns (with stale `latest`/`error` data). The board silently shows a mix of old and new data. Additionally `allGrouped` (line 74) is computed but never used — dead code that hints the intended merge logic was never implemented.
**Suggested fix:** Reconcile `columns` against `grouped` in an effect (add new fingerprints to `new`, drop fingerprints absent from `grouped`), or key the whole board state by the current filter/page so it resets per query.

### B3. `BoardView` — `move` uses stale `columns` closure
**File:** `BoardView.js`
**Lines:** 65–72
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `move` reads `columns` from the render closure. Two rapid drags (or a drag while a re-render is in flight) can drop a card: the second `setColumns` is computed from the pre-first-drag state, so the first move's card reappears in its old column or the second move's card is lost. Standard stale-closure bug with functional updates.
**Suggested fix:** Use `setColumns((prev) => …)` and compute the move from `prev`.

### B5. `MessageDetailDrawer` — conditional hook call
**File:** `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/messages/page.js`
**Lines:** 294–296 (`const { copyToClipboard } = useCopyToClipboard(); if (!message) return null;`)
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `useCopyToClipboard` is called before the early return, so the hook count is stable — this is actually **safe**. However, `MessageDetailDrawer` is always mounted (even when `message` is null), and `Drawer`'s `useEffect`s run with `isOpen=false` — fine. No violation here; flagging only that the pattern is fragile (any future hook added after the early return would break). Not a bug as written.

### B6. `Drawer` — Escape listener attached even when closed
**File:** `src/shared/components/Drawer.js`
**Lines:** 24–31
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** The `keydown` listener is attached whenever the component is mounted, regardless of `isOpen` (the guard is inside the handler). Since `MessageDetailDrawer` is always mounted, an Escape keypress anywhere on the page calls `onClose()` (a no-op `setSelected(null)` here, so harmless today) — but any future consumer with a side-effecting `onClose` would fire it while the drawer is closed. Also, the effect re-subscribes on every `onClose` identity change.
**Suggested fix:** Early-return `if (!isOpen) return;` inside the effect, or attach the listener only when `isOpen`.

### B7. `Drawer` — body scroll lock races with multiple drawers
**File:** `Drawer.js`
**Lines:** 12–22
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `document.body.style.overflow` is a single global. If two drawers are ever open (or one closes while another opens), the cleanup of one resets `overflow` while the other is still open, re-enabling page scroll behind the drawer. Fine for the single-drawer Messages page today, but a latent bug for the shared component.
**Fix:** Reference-count open drawers or use a stack.

## 2. Data bugs

### D1. `ConversationView` — `conversation.tokens` can be undefined → crash
**File:** `page.js`
**Lines:** 351–352 (`{fmtTokens(conversation.tokens.prompt + conversation.tokens.completion)} tok`)
**Severity:** **Major**
**Description:** The API builds `tokens` for conversations (route.js lines 60–66), so it's normally present. But `conversations` in the page also comes from `data?.conversations` — and the API's conversation projection only includes conversations whose rows appear in the **current page window** (see B3). If `tokens` is ever missing (older records, or a future API change), this throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prompt')` and crashes the whole page render. `TraceTreeView` has the same pattern (`c.tokens.prompt + c.tokens.completion`, line 62) — same crash risk.
**Fix:** `conversation.tokens?.prompt ?? 0`.

### B3. Conversation grouping is page-window-scoped — misleading counts
**File:** `src/app/api/messages/route.js`
**Lines:** 42–75 (grouping loop)
**Severity:** **Major**
**Description:** The comment says "Only conversations whose rows appear in this page's window" — so `messageCount` and `tokens` are **per-page**, not per-conversation. A conversation spanning 3 pages shows "2 msgs" on page 1, "5 msgs" on page 2, etc. The UI presents these as conversation totals ("X msgs · Y tok" in `ConversationView` and `TraceTreeView`), which is actively misleading. Also, a conversation whose messages are all on later pages is invisible in the Conversations/Trace views entirely.
**Fix:** Either compute conversation aggregates in SQL over the full filtered set (GROUP BY conversationId), or label the counts as "in this page".

### B4. `fmtLatency` — `total + "ms"` string concat on possibly-null
**File:** `page.js`
**Lines:** 111–116
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `latency.total ?? latency.totalMs` — if `total` is `0` (a real 0ms response), `fmtLatency` returns `"0ms"` (fine). But if `latency` is `{}` (the repo default `latency: item.latency || {}`), `total` is `undefined` → returns `"—"` (fine). No crash. However `total + "ms"` produces `"0ms"` for `0` — acceptable. The real issue: `latency.total` may be a **string** (if upstream code stores strings), producing `"123ms"` — cosmetic. **Minor at most; no crash.**

### B5. `fmtTokens` — `isNaN(n)` on non-number
**File:** `page.js` lines 96–101
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `isNaN(undefined)` is `true` → returns `"—"` (good). `isNaN(null)` is `false` → `null >= 1000000` is `false` → `String(null)` = `"null"` — displays "null" instead of "—". The `n == null` check at line 97 catches `null` first, so actually fine. **No bug.** (Verified: `n == null` short-circuits before `isNaN`.)

### B6. `extractText` — `b?.content` recursion can infinite-loop on circular refs
**File:** `page.js` lines 158–170; `export/route.js` lines 20–32
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `extractText` recurses on `b.content` with no depth guard. A self-referential block (or deeply nested content) would stack-overflow. Data comes from `truncateField`'d JSON so cycles are unlikely, but a depth cap is cheap insurance.

### B7. `buildCurl` (page) — `detail.providerRequest` may be a truncated marker
**File:** `page.js` lines 118–133
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `truncateField` (requestDetailsRepo.js lines 88–93) replaces oversized payloads with `{ _truncated: true, _originalSize, _preview }`. `buildCurl` then emits `-d '{ "_truncated": true, ... }'` — a misleading curl. Same in `export/route.js` `buildCurl` (lines 38–48). Should detect `_truncated` and note it.

## 3. Race conditions

### R1. **Filter-change fetch race — stale responses can overwrite newer ones**
**File:** `page.js`
**Lines:** 400–414 (`load`), 416–418 (`useEffect(() => { load(); }, [load])`)
**Severity:** **Major**
**Description:** `load()` has no cancellation or request sequencing. Typing in the Conversation ID input fires a fetch per keystroke (debounce absent); responses can arrive out of order, and the last-arriving (not last-issued) response wins. A slow response for filter A can overwrite the results for filter B. Also, `setLoading(true)` on every keystroke causes the whole table to flash "Loading…" — a UX bug.
**Fix:** AbortController per request (abort previous in `load`), or a monotonically increasing request id, plus debounce the conversationId input (~300ms).

### R2. Double-fetch on mount
**File:** `page.js`
**Lines:** 416–419
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `load` is in `useCallback` with deps `[page, pageSize, provider, status, conversationId]` — stable on mount, so the effect runs once. **No double-fetch on mount.** (Verified — the comment at line 415 claims "initial fetch triggered by the effect; subsequent from handlers", which is accurate.) However, `pageSize` is `useState(50)` with no setter — it's a constant; fine.

### R3. `openDetail` race — drawer shows stale message
**File:** `page.js`
**Lines:** 425–433
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `openDetail` fetches `/api/messages/${id}` and `setSelected(json.message)`. If the user clicks row A then quickly row B, the slower A response can land after B's, showing A's detail while B is highlighted. No request-id guard. Also `if (!res.ok) return;` silently swallows 404/500 — no error surface in the drawer.

## 4. Performance

### P1. **Facet queries run on every page/filter change — 5 GROUP BYs + full-window histogram scan**
**File:** `src/lib/db/repos/requestDetailsRepo.js`
**Lines:** 216–270 (`getRequestFacets`)
**Severity:** **Major**
**Description:** Every `GET /api/messages` (including every pagination click and keystroke-filter) runs 5 `GROUP BY` queries **plus** a full `SELECT timestamp, status FROM requestDetails WHERE …` over the entire filtered window (line 250) — the histogram is computed in JS over every matching row, not bucketed in SQL. With `maxRecords` default 200 this is fine, but the config allows up to `OBSERVABILITY_MAX_RECORDS` (unbounded) — at 100k+ rows this is a full table scan per request. The comment in the repo (lines 210–213) says the old code fetched "10k rows of JSON blobs (tens of MB)" — the histogram still fetches every row's timestamp+status, which is the same row count (just smaller payload). Also the histogram ignores the `page`/`pageSize` filter (correct — it's a global facet) but **does** apply provider/status filters, so the "last 24h" chart changes with filters — arguably intended.
**Fix:** Bucket the histogram in SQL (`strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:00', timestamp)` GROUP BY), and/or cache facets for a few seconds.

### P2. **Provider dropdown options derived from current page only**
**File:** `page.js`
**Lines:** 466–470
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** The provider `<select>` options are built from `messages` (the current page's rows). Providers not present on page 1 are unselectable, and the option list changes per page. The API already returns `facets.provider` (top 20 by count) — the page should use that instead. Also `getProviderName` is called per option per render — trivial, but the `filter((p,i,a) => …)` dedupe is O(n²) on a 50-row page — negligible.

### P3. `providerNameCache` module-level cache — never invalidated, and `fetchProviderNames` has no error handling
**File:** `page.js`
**Lines:** 24–38
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** If `/api/provider-nodes` fails (network blip), the promise rejects and `providerNames` stays `null` forever (the `.then` never runs; no `.catch`). The module cache also persists across route changes in the SPA — acceptable, but a failed first fetch is never retried. Also `providerNameCache`/`providerNodesCache` are module-level mutable state shared across all page instances — fine in practice.

## 5. UX bugs

### U1. **TimelineView scale when max=0 — division by zero**
**File:** `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/messages/components/TimelineView.js`
**Lines:** 38–42 (`maxTotal`), 96–97 (`ttftPct = ttft ? (ttft / max) * 100 : 0`)
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `maxTotal` returns `max || 1` (line 42), so `max` is never 0 — the guard is present and correct. However, `bodyPct = total ? ((total - ttft) / max) * 100 : 0` — if `total < ttft` (bad data), `bodyPct` is negative → `Math.max(negative, 2)` = 2% — fine. If `total === ttft` (no body), `bodyPct = 0` → `Math.max(0, 2)` = 2% — a phantom 2% body bar renders even when there's no body latency. **Minor visual bug:** a request with `total === ttft` shows a 2% body segment that doesn't exist. Also `ttft > total` (data anomaly) renders a body bar wider than the remaining space — bars can overflow the row.
**Fix:** Render body segment only when `total > ttft`, and clamp widths to `100%`.

### U2. **TimelineView — `ttft` fallback to `total` when ttft missing**
**File:** `TimelineView.js`
**Lines:** 28–33 (`latencyMetrics`)
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `total = typeof lat.total === "number" ? lat.total : (ttft || null)` — if `total` is missing but `ttft` exists, the whole bar is drawn as ttft (blue) and the body segment is skipped (`total > 0` true, `bodyPct = (total - ttft)/max = 0` → 2% phantom bar again). The row then shows `total` = ttft in the latency column, mislabeling ttft as total. Cosmetic but misleading.

### U3. **BoardView drag-drop — no drop on empty column area, no drag-over highlight**
**File:** `BoardView.js`
**Lines:** 96–120
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `onDrop` is only on the card elements, not the column container. Dropping onto the empty "Drop cards here" placeholder area (or anywhere in the column padding) does nothing — the placeholder div has no `onDrop`/`onDragOver`. Users will drag to the empty zone and the drop silently fails. Also no visual feedback on dragover (no `onDragEnter`/`onDragLeave` state), and `e.dataTransfer.setData("text/fp", …)` uses the generic `text/` MIME which some browsers sanitize; `text/plain` is safer. Also `onDragStart` doesn't `e.stopPropagation()` — nested drags are fine here, but the card's inner "View" button is a `<button>` inside a `draggable` div — clicking it may start a drag on some browsers (draggable on parent makes children draggable).
**Fix:** Put `onDragOver`/`onDrop` on the column container (and the placeholder), add visual drop-target feedback.

### U4. **List view — row click opens detail, but no loading/error state for the drawer fetch**
**File:** `page.js` lines 425–433, 520–525
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `openDetail` silently ignores failures (`catch {}`), so clicking a row with a failed fetch does nothing with no feedback. Also the drawer shows `message.timestamp` raw ISO string (line 307) while the list formats it — inconsistent.

### U5. **`ConversationView` — `open` state not reset when conversation changes**
**File:** `page.js` lines 274–292
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** Each `ConversationView` is keyed by `conversationId` (line 533), so state resets per conversation — fine. But the default `open=true` means every conversation renders all its messages expanded — with 50 messages per page and many conversations, the Conversations view renders a huge DOM. Minor perf/UX.

## 6. API bugs

### A1. **`GET /api/messages` — `page`/`pageSize` not clamped before use; `pageSize` default mismatch**
**File:** `src/app/api/messages/route.js`
**Lines:** 20–31
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `parseInt(searchParams.get("page"))` — `parseInt("abc")` = NaN → default 1 (good). But `pageSize` accepts up to 100 (validated), while the UI hardcodes 50. Fine. However, **`page` beyond `totalPages` returns an empty list with `hasNext: false`** — the client's `Pagination` component shows "Showing 0 to 0 of N" — acceptable. Real gap: **no validation of `startDate`/`endDate`** — `new Date("garbage").toISOString()` throws `RangeError` inside `buildWhere` (repo line 278–279), which is caught by the route's try/catch → 500 "Failed to fetch messages" instead of a 400. **Minor.**

### A2. **`GET /api/messages/[id]` — `params` is a Promise in Next 15; handled correctly**
**File:** `src/app/api/messages/[id]/route.js`
**Lines:** 15–16 (`const { id } = await params;`)
**Severity:** **None** (correct for Next 15+)
**Description:** Correctly awaits `params`. No bug. But note: `getRequestDetailById` returns the parsed `data` JSON — which includes `id` inside `data` (the record's `id` is stored in the `data` column too, per `flushToDatabase` line 133). The response spreads `{ ...detail, _id: id }` — so the message has both `id` and `_id`. The client uses `m.id || m._id` — consistent. **No bug**, but the `_id` is redundant.

### A3. **Export route — `format` is unvalidated; unknown formats silently return JSON**
**File:** `src/app/api/messages/[id]/export/route.js`
**Lines:** 66–90
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `format` defaults to `"json"` and any unknown value (e.g. `?format=html`) falls through to JSON with no error — a typo'd format returns JSON with a `Content-Type: application/json` — acceptable but should 400. Also `buildCurl` (lines 30–48) uses `detail.providerRequest?.url` — but the capture path (`flushToDatabase`) **never stores a URL** (the record has no `url` field; `providerRequest` is the payload). So `buildCurl` always emits `curl -X POST ""` — an empty URL. **This is a real bug**: the export curl is broken (empty URL), while the page's `buildCurl` (page.js line 122) hardcodes `"<provider-endpoint>/v1/chat/completions"` — also fake. Both are misleading exports.
**Fix:** Either capture the URL at save time, or emit a placeholder like the page does.

### A4. **`getRequestFacets` — `errorCategory`/`sourceApp` facets use `json_extract` but the WHERE clause for those filters also uses `json_extract` — consistent. However the facet GROUP BY on `json_extract(data, '$.errorCategory')` returns `null` for rows without the field, and the `.filter((r) => r.value !== null)` drops them — but `?? "unknown"` in the map (line 227) never fires because nulls are filtered after. So "unknown" facet never appears. Minor inconsistency with the `provider` facet which uses the column (NULL → "unknown" via `??`). Cosmetic.

### A5. **`getRequestDetails` — `ORDER BY timestamp DESC` with `LIMIT/OFFSET` — no tiebreaker**
**File:** `requestDetailsRepo.js` line 190
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** `timestamp` is TEXT ISO with ms precision — collisions are possible (two requests in the same ms, or the `generateDetailId` timestamp). Without a secondary sort key (`id`), pagination can skip/duplicate rows across pages when timestamps tie. Add `, id DESC` to the ORDER BY.

### A6. **`getRequestDetails` — `page` beyond range returns empty + `hasNext:false` — client keeps stale data**
**File:** `route.js` + `page.js`
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** If the user is on page 5 and applies a filter that reduces results to 1 page, the client sets `page(1)` in the filter handlers (page.js lines 460–464) — good. But the `Pagination` component's `onPageChange` (page.js line 530) doesn't clamp; if the API returns `pagination.page` > `totalPages` (e.g., data deleted between fetches), the UI shows an empty page with no "no results" message distinct from "no messages captured" (page.js line 512 shows the empty-state text even when filters are active — misleading: "No messages captured yet. Send a request…" appears when a filter simply has no matches).

### A7. **`GET /api/messages` — `conversationId` filter is exact-match only**
**File:** `route.js` line 36, repo `buildWhere` line 131
**Severity:** **Minor**
**Description:** The UI's Conversation ID input (page.js line 458) is a free-text field — users will paste a partial ID and get zero results. No `LIKE`/prefix matching. The empty-state message then says "No messages captured yet" — misleading.

### [2026-08-08T21:54:54.239Z] ASSISTANT ()

# Messages Page — Refactor & Design Decisions Report

## 1. Architecture: JSON-blob vs `messages` table

The current design is sound **at 200–1,000 records**: list queries use indexed columns (`requestDetailsRepo.js:214–221`, indexes at `schema.js:152–156`), and facets/histogram already run in SQL over the full set (`getRequestFacets`, `requestDetailsRepo.js:231–246`). The JSON-blob approach only degrades when rows exceed ~10k (the facet comment at `requestDetailsRepo.js:226` documents a prior tens-of-MB failure). **Don't migrate now; add a projection later.** The 3 biggest wins from the spec's `messages` table (`messages-page-feature-spec.md:33–70`):

1. **FTS5 search** — impossible over opaque `data` blobs without a searchable projection.
2. **`parent_message_id` trees/forks** — conversation grouping is currently rebuilt client-side from a page window only (`route.js:47–77`), so trees are truncated and cross-page forks are invisible.
3. **Denormalized cost/tokens/latency columns** — today's aggregation is a JS loop over fetched payloads; columns enable SQL GROUP BY rollups (session stats, P50/P95).

**Migration risk:** low — it's an additive table populated from the existing flush path (`requestDetailsRepo.js:104–141`); spec §3.7 already defines retention/backup exclusions. The real risk is **dual-write drift** (new `messages` rows vs legacy `requestDetails`), so gate population behind the same buffered writer and backfill lazily on read.

## 2. State management

Extract **`useMessagesQuery`** (custom hook, plain `useReducer` — no react-query dependency needed for a single-page local tool). Today's `page.js` has 10+ `useState` (`page.js:385–399`) plus an effect-driven fetch (`page.js:430`) that the React lint flags. The hook should own: filter state, `page`, loading/error, the `AbortController` race guard (already correctly handled at `page.js:402–428`), and derived view data. **Do not convert to server components** — this is a live-filterable, stateful dashboard page; App Router RSC adds no value here. Keep the drawer's per-record fetch (`openDetail`, `page.js:445`) as-is but move it into the hook with `useCallback`.

## 3. Component structure

Extract from the ~550-line `page.js`:

- `MessageRow` (table row, `page.js:575–611ow`   + `MessagesTable`
- `FilterBar` (`page.js:481–513`) — props-in/props-out, no state
- `FacetSidebar` — **new**, feeds the existing `facets` payload (`route.js:98`)
- `StatusBadge` + `STATUS_STYLES` (`page.js:31–53`) → `shared/components/` (duplicated across views)
- `FormatTabs` (`page.js:194–280`) → own file; `ConversationView` (`page.js:341–381`) → own file
- The `prettyJson`/`buildCurl`/`buildMarkdown` formatters are **duplicated** in `[id]/export/route.js:20–90` — extract to a shared `src/shared/messageFormats.js` used by both.

## 4. Design decisions

- **Roadmap:** P1 shipped (current state). Do **P2 (Error Inbox)** next — it's the highest-demand gap (HN/Sentry demand, spec §6) and reuses `/api/analyze-error`. P3 enrichment (headers/IP/taskType) enables the remaining filters; P4 ship-out last.
- **5-tab layout:** Keep tabs. The research (`message-viewer-design-philosophies.md:A.6`) confirms Pretty/Raw/Headers/cURL tabs are the universal expectation (Bruno/mitmweb/Hoppscotch). The 5 **view modes** (list/conversations/timeline/trace/board) correctly follow Linear's "views, not modes" (A.4).
- **FTS5 vs LIKE:** At <1k rows LIKE suffices; FTS5 wins at 10k+ and gives snippets/highlighting (recensa/claudex pattern). Build the `messages` table with FTS5 when you hit the projection, not before.
- **sourceApp fingerprinting:** `sourceApps.js` regex rules are **the right call** — the research explicitly endorses a "UA fingerprint → source app table" (`philosophies.md:C.3.2`), and `user-agent-parser` libs misclassify AI SDK UAs. Privacy is already correct: raw UA is capped at 300 chars and never stored (`sourceApps.js:55–58`), only the class — per D.4 guardrail. Keep it.

## 5. Real-world patterns

- **Sentry** (A.1): fingerprint-grouped issues + open/resolved/snoozed triage + frequency chart — adopt for the Board/Inbox. Avoid its ~20-container self-host weight.
- **Langfuse/LangSmith** (A.3): trace tree + session replay + denormalized per-span attributes — adopt; the "trace tree view" mirrors it.
- **Helicone** (synthesis §1.1): 9Router's twin — proves gateway+viewer is the right product shape; now in maintenance mode, so don't integrate, copy.
- **Datadog/OpenObserve** (A.2): facets-on-left + histogram-as-navigation — adopt; the current facet payload is ready for this.
- **Arize Phoenix**: skip — ELv2 license (synthesis §3 license guardrails).

````markdown
# Learning — Messages Page Audit & Refactor

**Date:** 2026-08-09
**Author:** GitHub Copilot agent
**Status:** active
**Tags:** #learning #messages #audit #refactor

## Summary

Full audit + bug-fix pass over the Messages page (`/dashboard/messages`,
`src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/messages/`) and its API surface
(`src/app/api/messages/*`). Six real bugs were found and fixed, a shared
formatting module was extracted to stop client/server drift, and a set of
deferred findings and future refactors were recorded.

## Audit Method

1. A **code-audit subagent** did the first sweep over `page.js`, the three view
   components (`BoardView`, `TimelineView`, `TraceTreeView`), the list route
   (`/api/messages`), and the detail/export routes (`/api/messages/[id]`,
   `/api/messages/[id]/export`), flagging every suspicious pattern with a
   reasoning tag (e.g. `R1` for the fetch race).
2. The **main session verified each finding** against the live code before any
   fix — no finding was accepted on the subagent's word alone. Fixes were then
   applied and re-checked against the same code.

This two-stage loop caught both false positives (dropped before fix) and real
bugs that a single pass tends to skim over (the BoardView state bug only
survives inspection when you trace both the render path and the filter-change
path).

## Bugs Found + Fixed

| # | Bug | Location | Root cause | Fix |
|---|-----|----------|-----------|-----|
| 1 | BoardView `setState`-during-render + stale columns | `components/BoardView.js` | Board kept the full column assignment in state and updated it during render; re-renders looped, and fingerprints from old pages/filters persisted on the board after the filter changed | State now holds **only user drag moves** (`moves: fp → column`); `grouped` and `columns` are derived with `useMemo`. New fingerprints land in "New", stale ones disappear with the filter/page |
| 2 | `conversation.tokens` null crash | `src/app/api/messages/route.js` | Conversation token/cost rollups assumed `tokens` was always present on every message; a record with `tokens: null` produced `NaN`/crash in rollup and in `ConversationView` rendering | Optional-chaining everywhere (`m.tokens?.prompt_tokens \|\| m.tokens?.input_tokens \|\| 0`) and rollups initialized to `{ prompt: 0, completion: 0 }` / `0` |
| 3 | Fetch race on filter change | `page.js` (`load`) | A slow response for an older filter could resolve after a newer request and overwrite newer results | One `AbortController` per `load()`; the previous request is aborted, `AbortError` is ignored, and `setLoading(false)` only runs if the controller is still current (`loadAbortRef.current === controller`) |
| 4 | cURL export: empty URL + truncated payloads | shared curl builder (old local copy in `page.js` / export route) | Capture never stores the upstream URL, so the old builder emitted `curl -X POST ""`; large bodies truncated at capture lost their truncation marker in export | `buildCurl` emits a `<provider-endpoint>/v1/chat/completions` placeholder and, when the body is truncated, prints `# NOTE: original payload was truncated at capture (N bytes)` + the `_preview` |
| 5 | TimelineView phantom body bar + ttft mislabeling | `components/TimelineView.js` | When `latency.ttft` was missing, `latencyMetrics` fell back to `0` ttft and the full total was rendered as a "body" bar — i.e. time-to-first-token mislabeled as streaming time | ttft defaults to `0` only when not a number; the body segment renders **only when real body latency exists** (`bodyMs = total && ttft < total ? total - ttft : 0`); the ttft segment only when `ttft > 0` |
| 6 | BoardView drop not working on column container | `components/BoardView.js` | Only cards had `onDrop`/`onDragOver`; dropping on the empty column container did nothing, and the container lacked `onDragOver` `preventDefault()` so the drop event never fired | The column container now has its own `onDragOver={e => e.preventDefault()}` + `onDrop` that reads `text/fp` + `text/from` from `dataTransfer` and calls `move()` |

## Other Findings (minor — deferred, not bugs at current scale)

| Finding | Notes |
|---------|-------|
| Facet queries are full-window scans | `getRequestFacets(filter)` GROUP BYs the entire filtered set on every request. Correct and fast at hundreds of rows; will need precomputed/rolled-up aggregates at scale |
| Provider dropdown options come from the current page's rows only | A provider with no message on this page is invisible in the filter dropdown; options should come from the full provider list or a facet |
| Drawer Escape listener registered while closed | The detail drawer's `keydown` listener is attached even when the drawer is closed; should be bound/unbound with the open state |
| body-scroll-lock multi-drawer race | Rapid open/close across multiple drawers can leave `body` scroll-locked |
| Pagination lacks a timestamp tiebreaker | `created_at`-only keyset ordering can skip/duplicate rows when two records share an identical timestamp; needs a `(created_at, id)` tiebreaker |
| Unknown export format silently returns JSON | `/api/messages/:id/export?format=bogus` falls through to the JSON default; should return a 400 instead |

## Refactor Done

Extracted **`src/shared/messageFormats.js`** — a single shared module exporting
`prettyJson`, `buildCurl`, `extractText`, and `buildMarkdown`. Both consumers
now import from it:

- `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/messages/page.js` (client) — imports
  `prettyJson`, `buildCurl`, `extractText` for the format tabs.
- `src/app/api/messages/[id]/export/route.js` (server) — imports `buildCurl`
  and `buildMarkdown` for `?format=curl|markdown`.

The functions are pure (no hooks, no browser APIs), so the `"use client"`
directive is safe for the page import and the route treats the module as a
normal server module. This kills the drift that previously let the page's curl
output and the export route's curl output disagree (empty URL, lost
truncation markers).

> Note: `buildMarkdown` on the page is intentionally kept **local** — the page
> renders a richer transcript (role-styled request messages + provider payload
> sections) than the export route's version. The shared module's `buildMarkdown`
> serves the export route. If the two ever converge, hoist the richer one.

## Recommended Future Refactors (from research)

1. **`useMessagesQuery` hook** — extract the `load()`/AbortController/filter
   state machine currently inlined in `MessagesPage` into a reusable hook
   (`page.js:360–395` is the shape).
2. **Component extraction** — pull `MessageRow`, `FilterBar`, and
   `FacetSidebar` out of the ~600-line `page.js` monolith.
3. **`StatusBadge` → shared components** — move to `src/shared/components/`
   so the usage page / error inbox reuse it (`STATUS_STYLES` map is the
   canonical one).
4. **`messages` table projection at scale** — when `requestDetails` passes
   ~10k rows, introduce the thin `messages` projection with FTS5 +
   `parent_message_id` trees per the feature spec — see
   `../decisions/ADR-007-messages-json-blob-vs-messages-table.md`.
5. **P2 Error Inbox** — next feature on the roadmap
   (`plans/messages-page-feature-spec.md` §6); the BoardView fingerprint
   grouping is its foundation.

- Research: `../research/message-viewer-design-philosophies.md`
- ADR: `../decisions/ADR-007-messages-json-blob-vs-messages-table.md`
- Files: `src/shared/messageFormats.js`, `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/messages/`
  (`page.js`, `components/BoardView.js`, `components/TimelineView.js`),
  `src/app/api/messages/route.js`, `src/app/api/messages/[id]/export/route.js`
````

## File 2 → `docs/plans-and-prompts/decisions/ADR-007-messages-json-blob-vs-messages-table.md`

````markdown
# ADR-007: Messages Page — JSON-Blob Store vs. Dedicated `messages` Table

**Date:** 2026-08-09
**Author:** GitHub Copilot agent (main session)
**Status:** active
**Tags:** #decision #messages #data-model #sqlite #observability

## Context

The Messages page (`/dashboard/messages`,
`src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/messages/page.js` + `src/app/api/messages/*`)
reads traffic directly from **`requestDetails`** — the JSON-blob store
(`src/lib/db/schema.js`: `id TEXT PK, timestamp, provider, model,
connectionId, status, data JSON, conversationId`) — via
`getRequestDetails(filter)` and `getRequestFacets(filter)`.

The feature spec (`plans/messages-page-feature-spec.md` §3) proposes a
**hybrid relational pattern**: a thin searchable `messages` table
(`session_id`, `request_id`, `role`, `model`, `parent_message_id`, `status`,
`tokens`, `latency_ms`, `created_at` + indexes) as a *projection* of the fat
wire-faithful JSON bodies, with an **FTS5** virtual table for search and
cost columns for rollups. `requestDetails` stays the payload store.

This ADR settles which store the page queries **now**.

## Decision

**Keep the JSON-blob store (`requestDetails`) as the Messages page's query
store.** Do **not** create the `messages` projection table yet. Add it later,
gated on scale — revisit when `requestDetails` exceeds ~10k rows or when an
FTS5/cost-rollup feature is actually shipped.

## Why

- **Current scale is sound.** At the observed 200–1,000 record range every
  query the page issues is an indexed-column lookup or a small scan of an
  indexed table: `getRequestDetails(filter)` filters on `provider`, `model`,
  `status`, `conversationId`, and timestamp; `errorCategory`/`sourceApp` are
  filtered **in SQL via JSON1** so pagination math stays correct with no
  client-side post-filtering.
- **The "facets in SQL" requirement is already met.** `getRequestFacets`
  computes facet counts with `GROUP BY` over the full filtered set — no row
  payloads shipped, counts correct across pages. A relational table would not
  change this code path.
- **JSON-blob is the wire-fidelity source of truth (P1).** It preserves exact
  translated payloads, thinking blocks, and fallback attempts. A projection
  necessarily duplicates that and adds a second thing that can drift.
- **Dual-write drift risk outweighs the benefit at this scale.** The spec's
  population path (write from the buffered-writer flush) introduces
  dual-write drift — stream retries, dedupe by message `id`, partial writes —
  with **zero user-visible benefit** while the page is fast on the blob.
  Migration risk alone is low; dual-write risk is the real cost.

## Consequences

**Positive:**
- No new table, no migration, no dual-write path to keep in sync.
- JSON1 blob queries remain the single source of truth; page stays fast at
  current scale.
- Schema churn deferred until a real problem exists, not speculative.

**Negative (accepted):**
- No FTS5 full-text search — search is substring/regex-level for now.
- Conversation trees are assembled in JS from `conversationId` grouping, not
  from `parent_message_id` (no forking trees yet).
- Cost rollups are computed per-query in JS from `tokens`/`cost` fields.
- Facet queries scan the full filtered window (fine today; revisit at scale).

**Operational:**
- `requestDetails` retention janitor (`observabilityMaxRecords`, LIMIT-based
  sweep) remains the only cleanup path; keep the same exclusion in backups
  (`src/lib/db/backup.js`).

## When to Revisit

Introduce the `messages` projection table when **any** of these hit:

1. **Scale:** `requestDetails` grows past ~10k rows — pagination latency and
   facet scans degrade; keyset pagination on a thin table becomes the fix.
2. **Search:** FTS5 in-conversation search becomes a shipped requirement
   (spec §4 "Search").
3. **Cost rollups:** dashboard-level cost aggregates needed at scale — add
   precomputed/aggregate columns or a rollup table.
4. **Error Inbox (P2):** before building it, revisit — the inbox needs
   `status`/`errorCategory` aggregates and fingerprint queries that a thin
   table with `idx_msg_status` serves far better.

## Alternatives Rejected

- **Immediate migration to the spec's `messages` table** — dual-write drift
  risk (stream retries, dedupe, partial flush writes) with no user-visible
  benefit at 200–1,000 records; also FTS5/parent-tree features it would serve
  are not yet shipped.
- **Replace the blob store with fully normalized tables** — breaks wire
  fidelity (P1), the entire reason the blob exists.
- **Read-only projection rebuilt on demand** (derived table, not dual-write)
  — same drift/maintenance burden as the dual-write path with no scale driver
  today.

## Related

- Spec: `../plans/messages-page-feature-spec.md`
- Research: `../research/message-viewer-design-philosophies.md`
- Learning (audit + refactor session): `../learnings/2026-08-09-messages-page-audit-and-refactor.md`
- Files: `src/app/api/messages/route.js`, `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/messages/page.js`, `src/lib/usageDb.js` (`getRequestDetails` / `getRequestFacets`)
````

### [2026-08-10T03:11:25.528Z] ASSISTANT ()

**Scrutiny found 3 real bugs + 1 hygiene issue**:

1. **CRITICAL — client-abort crash**: `req` (IncomingMessage) has no `'error'` handler. A client disconnecting mid-request (common with streaming) emits `ECONNRESET` → unhandled stream error → **proxy process crashes** — the exact failure this proxy exists to prevent.
2. **CRITICAL — upstream mid-stream reset crash**: `pres` has no `'error'` handler either — app killed mid-SSE → crash.
3. **HIGH — stale-probe race**: `tick()` can outlive the 2s interval (3s probe timeout), so a slow tick started earlier can overwrite newer state with stale results.
4. **MEDIUM — hop-by-hop headers** (`connection`, `transfer-encoding`, `upgrade`, etc.) forwarded per RFC 7230 §6.1 — can double-frame chunked bodies or pass h2c upgrades brokenly.

Applying all fixes:

All tasks complete. Here's the full rundown:

## ✅ Node Failover — Implemented, Tested, Deployed

**What was built** (`cli/failover-proxy.cjs`, zero dependencies):
- Health-probes local + peer every 2s (`/api/health`, any status <500 = up)
- Routes **local-preferred / peer-backup** — peer only used when local is dead
- `x-9r-failover` loop protection, SSE-safe bidirectional streaming, 120s upstream timeout, both-down → fail-open to local with the app's real error

**Local harness** (T1–T5): failover, failback, loop protection, both-down — all green.

**Real-world testing (mini-2 ↔ mini2)** — full matrix verified:
| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Kill mini-2's app | its proxy kept serving from mini2 (identity-proven via `requireLogin`) |
| Kill mini2's app | its proxy kept serving from mini-2 |
| Both restored | both proxies failed back to local |
| `/v1/chat/completions` through proxy during kill | structured app response — endpoint continuity, no connection refused |
| Streaming | clean through the proxy |

**Scrutiny pass** (as you requested) — found and fixed **3 real bugs**:
1. 🔴 Unhandled `error` on client request → a client abort (streaming cancel!) **crashed the proxy** — now tears down upstream instead
2. 🔴 Unhandled `error` on upstream response → app killed mid-stream (the failover scenario itself!) **crashed the proxy**
3. 🟠 Stale-probe race — a slow tick could overwrite newer health state → monotonic sequence guard
Plus hop-by-hop header hygiene (RFC 7230 §6.1). Re-verified the whole matrix + crash-resilience tests, redeployed hardened build to both machines.

# Research Report: B3, B4, and Error Inbox P2

## Summary of current state

**B3 (conversation grouping) is already DONE** — it was resolved 2026-08-09 (TASK-LOG §102–104, commit `feat(messages): DB-level conversation aggregation + keyset pagination`). Only B4 and Error Inbox P2 remain open, plus the B4-related "4.3/4.4 user-owned" items. No partial work exists for B4 or Error Inbox (no `/api/messages/conversations` endpoint, no error-inbox page, no fingerprint column/persistence).

## Item 1: B3 — Conversation grouping is page-scoped

### Current implementation (already global)

The page-scoping was **fixed**. Conversation grouping now happens in SQL over the **full filtered dataset**, not the page window:

- **`src/lib/db/repos/requestDetailsRepo.js:531` — `getConversationSummary(filter)`**: `GROUP BY COALESCE(conversationId, '(none)')` over the entire filtered set with `COUNT(*)`, token sums (`json_extract(data,'$.tokens.prompt_tokens')` with `input_tokens` fallback), cost sums, `MIN/MAX(timestamp)`. Pagination now refers to the **conversation list** (distinct conversations), not rows.
- **`requestDetailsRepo.js:591` — `getConversationMessages(conversationId, filter)`**: full thread ASC (`timestamp ASC, id ASC`), `pageSize` capped at 500, `conversationId=null` → the `"(none)"` group.
- **`src/app/api/messages/route.js:77-97`**: `view=conversations` → calls `getConversationSummary`; pagination swapped to the conversation list (`nextCursor = null`, page-by-number); a `conversationId` param attaches the full thread via `getConversationMessages` regardless of page window.
- **`route.js:98-140`**: for list/timeline/trace views, a lightweight page-window projection still groups rows, but a selected `conversationId` always fetches its **full thread** (B3 note at line 128-132).
- **`src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/messages/page.js:411-455`**: Conversations view pages by number with "Load more" appending non-duplicate conversations; threads lazy-load on expand (`loadThread` → `conversationId` param → full thread). Keyset cursor pagination for the flat list landed in the same commit (opaque `timestamp|id` base64url cursor, `(timestamp < ? OR (timestamp = ? AND id < ?))` tiebreak, `pageSize+1` lookahead).
- **Tests**: `tests/unit/conversation-keyset.test.js` (12 tests) covers multi-page conversations (25 rows spanning pages), token/cost correctness, `(none)` grouping, pagination, keyset walk, timestamp-tie id tiebreak. Suite: 1772 pass / 86 fail (budget ≤ 89).

### What's needed
**Nothing for B3 itself.** It is complete and tested. If anything, the only conceivable follow-up is the R1 research note (defer a `messages` table until ~10k rows; ADR-007) — explicitly **deferred by design**.

### Gotchas
- `getConversationSummary` intentionally ignores `conversationId` in its filter (grouping *by* conversation) — `buildWhere({ ...filter, conversationId: undefined })`.
- The `"(none)"` sentinel: rows with NULL `conversationId` group under `'(none)'`, returned as `null` in JSON; the client uses `conv.conversationId ?? "(none)"` as the map key.
- FTS5 index (`requestDetails_fts`) is kept in sync in the same flush transaction; the janitor `DELETE FROM requestDetails_fts WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM requestDetails)` is **not** affected by conversation grouping.

### Recommendation
**Defer / no action.** Already implemented. Close the TASK-LOG item.

## Item 2: B4 — cURL URL capture

### Current implementation

- **`src/shared/messageFormats.js:20-38` — `buildCurl(detail)`**: emits hardcoded `curl -X POST "<provider-endpoint>/v1/chat/completions"` placeholder, plus `-H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"`, truncated-payload note, and a trailing `# Provider/Model/Account` comment block. The comment explicitly says *"The capture path never stores the upstream URL"*.
- **`src/app/api/messages/[id]/export/route.js`**: `?format=curl` calls `buildCurl(detail)` from `getRequestDetailById`.

### (a) Is the upstream URL available at capture time? **Yes.**

The chat pipeline already computes and holds the exact upstream URL in a local variable:

- **`open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js:334-342`**: `let providerResponse, providerUrl, providerHeaders, finalBody;` — the executor's `execute()` returns `{ response, url, headers, transformedBody }`, captured into `providerUrl` (and re-set on the token-refresh retry path at line ~405).
- **`open-sse/executors/base.js` `execute()`** (default executor): `return { response, url, headers, transformedBody };` where `url = this.buildUrl(model, stream, urlIndex, credentials)` (retry/fallback URLs handled in the loop).
- `open-sse/executors/default.js` overrides `buildUrl` with the runtime-transport/gemini/urlSuffix/`{accountId}` logic — all paths return a concrete full URL.
- **`clientRawRequest.endpoint` is NOT the upstream URL** — it's the *9Router's own* route pathname (`src/sse/handlers/chat.js:45`: `endpoint: url.pathname`, i.e. `/v1/chat/completions`). This is already passed as an override in two handlers (`nonStreamingHandler.js:395` and `sseToJsonHandler.js:225,318` as `{ endpoint: clientRawRequest?.endpoint || null }`), but that's the client-facing endpoint, not what curl needs. The true upstream URL lives only in `providerUrl`, a local in `chatCore.js`, which is **not** currently threaded into the sub-handlers.

### Capture call sites (all 8)
| File:line | Status | Has providerUrl in scope? |
|---|---|---|
| `chatCore.js:352` (executor throw) | error | **Yes** (in scope) |
| `chatCore.js:420` (provider error `!response.ok`) | error | **Yes** (in scope) |
| `streamingHandler.js:78` (non-SSE blocked) | error | No — but could pass from chatCore |
| `streamingHandler.js:111` (stream start) | success | No |
| `streamingHandler.js:148` (stream complete via `buildOnStreamComplete`) | success | No |
| `nonStreamingHandler.js:374` | success | No (uses `clientRawRequest?.endpoint`) |
| `sseToJsonHandler.js:221` (Responses SSE→JSON) | success | No (uses `clientRawRequest?.endpoint`) |
| `sseToJsonHandler.js:314` (chat-completions SSE→JSON) | success | No (uses `clientRawRequest?.endpoint`) |

### (b) Minimal change to thread it through

1. **`open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js`**: add `providerUrl` to the two error capture sites (`buildRequestDetail({ ..., url: providerUrl || null })` or via overrides). Add `providerUrl` to `sharedCtx` (line ~457) so it flows into all sub-handlers (`handleStreamingResponse`, `buildOnStreamComplete`, `handleNonStreamingResponse`, `handleForcedSSEToJson`).
2. **`open-sse/handlers/chatCore/requestDetail.js` `buildRequestDetail`**: add `url: base.url || overrides.url || undefined` to the returned detail (like `errorCategory`/`sourceApp` — pass-through).
3. **Sub-handlers** (`streamingHandler.js` ×3, `nonStreamingHandler.js` ×1, `sseToJsonHandler.js` ×2): add `url: providerUrl` (or thread it into `sharedCtx`'s destructure).
4. **`requestDetailsRepo.js` `flushToDatabase`** (line ~217-238): the record whitelist builds `record` with explicit fields + JSON blob. Add `url: item.url || null` to the whitelist so it's persisted inside `data`. **No schema change needed** — `data` is a TEXT JSON blob; nothing is filtered on `url`, so no column/index/migration.
5. **`messageFormats.js` `buildCurl`**: `const endpoint = detail.url || "<provider-endpoint>/v1/chat/completions";` and use `endpoint` in the first line.

### (c) Persisted-field whitelist (flushToDatabase)
Current record fields (`requestDetailsRepo.js:217-238`): `id, provider, model, connectionId, timestamp, status, latency, tokens, request, providerRequest, providerResponse, response, pxpipe, conversationId, errorCategory, sourceApp, userAgent, cost, costProvenance, pricingModel`. All stored in the `data` JSON column. `url` would be a new field — additive, no migration.

### Gotchas
- **The `endpoint` override already used in two handlers is the *client* endpoint, not upstream** — don't confuse them. The correct value is `providerUrl` from `chatCore.js` scope.
- **Token-refresh retry**: `providerUrl` is reassigned in the retry block; the final value is correct to persist.
- **Legacy rows**: old records lack `url` — `buildCurl` must keep the placeholder fallback (backward-compat; no backfill needed).
- **Test impact**: `tests/unit/error-category-detail.test.js` and `cost-capture.test.js` assert on `buildRequestDetail` output shape; adding `url: undefined` when absent preserves backward compat (the pattern used for `errorCategory`). No known test asserts the placeholder string in `buildCurl`; a small test addition is advisable.
- **Privacy**: the URL may contain account IDs (`{accountId}` in base.js/default.js `buildUrl`). Fine to store — it's already logged in the request logger (`reqLogger.logTargetRequest(providerUrl, ...)`).

### Recommendation
**Implement now.** It's small (≈6 one-line changes + 1 whitelist addition), the URL is already available at capture time, no schema/migration risk, and it completes the "error sweep" E-item (B4). The only nuance is threading `providerUrl` through `sharedCtx` and being careful not to use `clientRawRequest.endpoint`.

## Item 3: Error Inbox P2

### Current implementation

- **Error categorization — `open-sse/utils/errorCategorizer.js`** (`categorizeError(status, text)`): pure function, 8 stable categories: `rate_limit | auth | billing | timeout | overloaded | content_filter | invalid_request | network | unknown`. Rules checked top-to-bottom: status match is decisive; text regex fallback; `s>=500 → overloaded`, `s>=400 → invalid_request`, else `unknown`.
- **`open-sse/config/errorConfig.js`**: separate concern — `ERROR_TYPES` (HTTP→OpenAI error type/code mapping), `ERROR_RULES` (cooldown/backoff classification for the retry/cooldown engine), `COOLDOWN_MS`. This is the *retry/cooldown* config, **not** the category taxonomy. `errorCategory` (as stored on records) comes from `errorCategorizer.js`, not `errorConfig.js`.
- **Where `errorCategory` is set at capture**: all error capture sites call `categorizeError(status, message)` (chatCore.js:356, 424, streamingHandler.js:80, etc.). Stored in `requestDetails.data.errorCategory`; also a JSON1 SQL filter (`buildWhere` → `json_extract(data, '$.errorCategory') = ?`) and a facet (`getRequestFacets` → `countGroup("json_extract(data, '$.errorCategory')")`).
- **BoardView — `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/messages/components/BoardView.js`**: groups by **client-side** fingerprint = `provider|model|errorCategory|normalizedError.slice(0,120)` (hash via `fingerprint(m)` at line 28-37). Columns New/Investigating/Resolved/Snoozed; drag moves are **local state only** (`moves` map), explicitly *"no persistence yet — P2"* (line 48). `normalizeError` at line 43 slices to 100 chars for display.
- **Existing related asset**: `src/app/api/analyze-error/route.js` — POST `{detailId}` → runs `handleChatCore` with a diagnostic prompt to analyze one failure (settings `analyzeErrorModel`, default `oc/mimo-v2.5-free`). This is the per-issue "analyze" hook an error inbox can reuse.

### What a P2 Error Inbox needs (concrete, minimal)

Two sub-pieces:

**A. Aggregation API (server):** Add a fingerprint-grouping query to `requestDetailsRepo.js` mirroring the `getConversationSummary` pattern (SQL GROUP BY over full filtered set):
- Add `fingerprint` computed in the GROUP BY as `provider || '|' || COALESCE(model,'') || '|' || COALESCE(json_extract(data,'$.errorCategory'),'') || '|' || <normalized error>` — but **normalized error is hard to normalize in SQL**. Practical approach: group by `provider | model | errorCategory` in SQL (server-side, exact), then fold the error text client-side (as BoardView already does) for display, OR persist a fingerprint at capture. A dedicated `errorInbox`-style endpoint could live under `/api/messages/errors` or as a `view=errors` mode on the existing route (no new route needed — the route already filters `status=error` + `errorCategory` and returns facets).
- Filter by `status=error` (column, indexed) + optional `errorCategory` (JSON1).
- Aggregate: `COUNT(*)`, `MIN/MAX(timestamp)`, `MIN(error)`, `SUM(cost)`, `errorCategory`.

**B. Persistence of column assignments (the bigger ask):** BoardView's drag assignments are local-only. Options:
1. **Settings/DB store** (`src/lib/db/repos/settingsRepo.js` exists): a `KV`-style map `boardColumns: { [fp]: columnKey }`. Minimal — reuse the `kv` table (`getSetting/setSetting`), no schema change. This is the smallest viable persistence (triage state survives reload/restart).
2. **A proper issue/inbox table** (spec's `messages` table or a new `inboxIssues` table): fingerprint rows with status, assignee, notes, snooze-until. More work; arguably P3.

The design doc's R4 and the messages-page feature spec both point to **P2 = Error Inbox next**, reusing `/api/analyze-error`. The roadmap says "P2 (Error Inbox) next" with Sentry-style fingerprint-grouped issues + triage + frequency chart.

### Gotchas
- **Fingerprint stability**: the current BoardView fingerprint includes the raw error text (sliced to 120) — a tiny message variation creates a new fingerprint. For aggregation across records you want the **coarser** `provider|model|errorCategory` key (Sentry-style) with the error text as *display*, not part of the key. That's a deliberate design choice to make.
- **`errorConfig.js` vs `errorCategorizer.js`**: don't build the inbox on `ERROR_RULES`/`ERROR_TYPES` — those are cooldown/backoff config. The category strings on records come from `errorCategorizer.js`. (The user prompt cited `errorConfig.js`; the actual category source is `errorCategorizer.js`.)
- **SQL vs client grouping**: current BoardView groups client-side over the *page window only* — the same page-scoping bug B3 fixed for conversations. The Error Inbox must aggregate server-side (SQL GROUP BY) or it'll undercount.
- **JSON1 filter performance**: `errorCategory` filter is `json_extract(data,...)` — fine at current 200–1k row scale; at 10k+ the R1 messages-table migration (ADR-007) is the fix, which is where real inbox schema lives.
- **Dual-write risk**: if you persist column assignments in settings AND later migrate to a messages table, the fingerprint→column map must be keyed stably (the coarse key), otherwise drift. Use the coarse key from day one.
- **Rate-limit/cooldown coupling**: `categorizeError` ignores cooldown state; don't mix inbox triage with the cooldown engine's state.

### Recommendation
**Implement now, in two slices** (matches the documented roadmap):
1. **Slice 1 (small)**: server-side fingerprint aggregation — add a `getErrorSummary(filter)` SQL GROUP BY to `requestDetailsRepo.js` (mirror `getConversationSummary`), expose via the existing `/api/messages` route (`view=errors` + `status=error`) or a tiny new `/api/messages/errors` route; keep the current `provider|model|errorCategory` key. Reuses existing facets/filters, no schema change.
2. **Slice 2 (medium)**: persist BoardView column moves in the `kv`/settings store (`boardColumns` map keyed by the coarse fingerprint). This converts the board from a demo into a usable inbox. Optionally wire the existing `/api/analyze-error` per-issue "Analyze" button into the board cards (it already exists end-to-end).

Defer only the full issue-entity schema (notes/assignees/snooze-until) until the ADR-007 messages-table migration triggers.

# v0.5.50 (2026-08-05)

## Features
- **Providers**: add TokenRouter (300+ models via OpenAI-compatible gateway) with
  exact per-model pricing for 110 models and `reasoning_effort` thinking config
- **Providers**: add Self-hosted STT / TTS / Embedding — point 9Router at your own
  OpenAI-compatible speech and embedding servers (whisper.cpp, faster-whisper,
  Kokoro-FastAPI, llama-server, vLLM, Infinity). Unlike the named cloud providers
  these read `baseUrl` per connection, so one provider can front several machines
- **Combos**: default-enable vision/audio capacity adapter (auto-routes to a
  vision/audio-capable model when the target lacks that capability, falling back
  to `oc/mimo-v2.5-free`), wired into chat handler routing
- **Endpoint**: auto-provision a "Default Key" for first-time users so `/v1`
  works without a manual dashboard step
- **Codex**: support GPT-5.6 Max/Ultra reasoning-level overrides (cx/ routes only)
- **Qoder**: support PAT (Personal Access Token) connections end-to-end, alongside
  OAuth device flow
- **CLI tools**: add OpenDesign (manalkaff/opendesign) support
- **Headroom**: report effective payload savings (tool schema/history bytes broken
  out, byte-savings % reflects actual outbound reduction)
- **Ollama**: Cloud quota tracker (session + weekly) + proactive background OAuth
  token refresh scheduler for all providers

## Fixes
- **Providers**: remove Qwen (OAuth flow stopped working reliably)

### Verification (real world, mini-2 ↔ mini2)
- Local harness: failover/failback/loop-protection/both-down all green.
- Real world: killed each node's app in turn — the proxy on the down node kept
  serving from the peer (attributed via `requireLogin` identity marker);
  `/v1/chat/completions` through the proxy returned structured app errors (not
  connection refused); failback verified after both restores.
- Both proxies deployed on :20142 (mini-2 → local :20130/peer mini2 :20128;
  mini2 → local :20128/peer 192.168.1.154:20130).

### fix(failover): post-implementation scrutiny — 3 real bugs (2026-08-09)
- S11/S12 CRITICAL: unhandled `'error'` on client request + upstream response —
  client abort or app-killed-mid-stream crashed the proxy. Now tears down the
  upstream pair instead.
- S13 HIGH: stale-probe race (slow tick overwriting newer state) → monotonic
  `tickSeq` guard.
- S14 MEDIUM: hop-by-hop headers forwarded (RFC 7230 §6.1) → stripped.
- S15 MEDIUM: client closed mid-body → teardown on incomplete `close`.
- S16 LOW: empty 502 detail on Node 22 → `e.code || e.message || e.name`.
- Re-verified: T1–T5 matrix + C1/C2 crash-resilience tests pass; hardened build
  redeployed to both machines (final matrix 200/200/200/200).

/** Extract plain text from a content value of any shape (string/array/blocks). */
export function extractText(content, depth = 0) {
  if (content == null) return "";
  if (typeof content === "string") return content;
  if (depth > 10) return ""; // guard against deep/circular structures
  if (Array.isArray(content)) {
    return content
      .map((b) => {
        if (typeof b === "string") return b;
        if (b?.text) return b.text;
        if (b?.content) return extractText(b.content, depth + 1);
        return "";
      })
      .join("\n");
  }
  return "";
}

/** Render a captured request as a Markdown transcript. */
export function buildMarkdown(detail) {
  const out = [];
  out.push(`## ${detail.timestamp || "unknown"} — ${detail.provider || "unknown"}/${detail.model || "unknown"} [${detail.status || "unknown"}]`);
  out.push("");
  if (detail.conversationId) out.push(`- **Conversation:** \`${detail.conversationId}\``);
  if (detail.connectionId) out.push(`- **Account:** \`${detail.connectionId}\``);
  if (detail.errorCategory) out.push(`- **Category:** \`${detail.errorCategory}\``);
  const lat = detail.latency;
  if (lat) out.push(`- **Latency:** ttft=${lat.ttft ?? "?"}ms total=${lat.total ?? "?"}ms`);
  const tok = detail.tokens;
  if (tok) out.push(`- **Tokens:** in=${tok.prompt_tokens ?? tok.input_tokens ?? "?"} out=${tok.completion_tokens ?? tok.output_tokens ?? "?"}`);
  out.push("");
  const reqMsgs = detail.request?.messages || detail.request?.input || [];
  if (reqMsgs.length) {
    out.push("### Request");
    out.push("```json");
    out.push(JSON.stringify(reqMsgs, null, 2));
    out.push("```");
